docs.title: Platform glossary: the terms the eight specifications share, and where each is defined
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-26 at 9ea0af8cd.

Contributor-facing. Living, current at main 5a9a49cc (2026-10-18). Each term links to where it is specified; the definition here is a summary, and the linked section is the authority. Therapy terms (profile, override, temporary target) are in the domain glossary. The platform index explains the layers.

HS below is the hub-sync design, REG the registration specification and ID the identity specification; WC is the write contract.

docs.title: "Primitive" has three meanings
docs.text:
The word appears across the series for three different things. Use the qualified term.

say meaning where observation primitive a typed record kind such as SensorGlucose, Bolus or ApsSnapshot that a composite document decomposes into specs/sync/primitives.yaml; HS §3.3 grammar member a member of the registration grammar (stateSpans, extensions, settings, a type fragment) REG §3; specs/sync/controller-state-model.schema.json contract primitive a building block of the hub contract: an id, a definition, an instance, a role, an etag, a write result this glossary, L0, L2 and L5

docs.title: L0 Identity
docs.text:
_id. The storage key the hub assigns. On every hub's legacy surface (API v1 and v3) it is a 24-hex value, on MongoDB and PostgreSQL alike. Its first four bytes are the hub's receipt time, not the record's time. ID I2, I3.

identifier. The sync identity the client assigns, stable across retries and devices. In the typed API it is the controller's record id. A UUID is recommended, not required. The proposed constraints are in identifier format §0, and the format decision is open (ID-FORMAT-DECISION).

Two-id rule. Every write reply returns both identifier and _id and says which one matched (matchedBy). A re-send matches on identifier first, then on _id, so a client needs no cache of server ids. ID I4, I5.

syncIdentifier. A controller's own per-record sync key (Loop and LoopKit; Nocturne's V4 update key is (dataSource, syncIdentifier)). It is not unique per record in stored data: 13 Loop values each appear on 2 to 4 treatments (identifier duplicates). A controller may send it as identifier.

Natural key. The fields a re-send without an id is matched on, one key per collection on every write path: entries date+type, profile created_at, treatments created_at+eventType; devicestatus created_at+device for an identical body only; food and activity by id only. Today the key differs by path. Identity §3.

Definition id. sha256: and the hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of a definition as submitted. Equal content gives an equal id. ID §2.

Instance id. A random lowercase UUID v4 the controller generates once per running copy. It is never derived from a device name, model or serial. ID §2.

Subject. The opaque id of the principal a credential belongs to. Tokens rotate; the subject does not. Registrations and instances bind to the subject, never to a token.

docs.title: L1 Records
docs.text:
Specified in the records specification.

Composite document, carrier. Today's wire documents (a treatment, a devicestatus, a profile). A carrier is the composite shape an element is written in when it is not written typed: its wire declaration (collection, eventType, duration unit, indefinite sentinel, how "ended" is encoded).

Decomposition. Turning a composite document into observation primitives on write, keeping the composite as well. D11.

Evidence grade. measured (a wire path in the corpus populates it), declared (a typed model has it and the corpus does not show it), proposed (asked for). In registrations, evidence is read (from source) or measured.

Quirk. A recorded way stored documents deviate from the documented shape, scoped by affects: {vendor, product, versions}, with a lifecycle proposed → active → historical → retired. quirks registry; REG §16.

Sensitivity label. A field's two-axis label (specs/sync/sensitivity.yaml). A field with no label is withheld by default (unlabelledPolicy: withhold).

Horizon. How long a value stays meaningful: cycle, span, effective-dated, definition or aggregate, each with its own cadence and retention.

docs.title: L2 Definitions and instances
docs.text:
Registration, product. A controller's declaration of what its data means, one per (vendor, product) per tenant. The product resource holds the binding, the state (active, retired, blocked), the etag and the per-element results. REG §5.

Tier. Well-known: registrations the hub ships for controllers that declare nothing, so legacy writers need no change. Controller-owned: registrations a controller submits. D18.

Capability document. GET /.well-known/nightscout/sync: unauthenticated and cacheable. It says which grammar majors, members, type keywords, horizons, limits, roles and shared slots the hub supports. It never lists a tenant's registrations.

Element, element result. The unit the hub accepts or rejects: a stateSpans kind, an extension namespace, a typed settings field or a typed replay input. The result is accepted, accepted-with-ignored-members or rejected with reasons. A registration is accepted or partial overall.

Fallback. What a controller writes when an element is not accepted: the element's carrier. Decided per element, from the response to this registration only.

Definition. An immutable, content-addressed statement of what a controller's data means. Many coexist under one product; ten simulators on one build share one. D19.

Meaning members, version-conflict. The members of a kind, extension or field that define what it means (REG §7's table). Within one product, one element at one version has one meaning. A different meaning at the same version is rejected version-conflict; a new meaning needs a new version.

Instance. One running copy of a controller (a phone that doses, a development build, a simulator, the old and new phone during a migration). It names its definition, holds roles on channels and renews a lease. REG §8.

Lease. An instance's liveness. Each create or renewal extends it by the hub's instances.leaseSeconds; an instance that stops renewing lapses and holds no roles.

Label. A string key and value on an instance, <reverse-DNS namespace>/<name>, for selecting and filtering. dev.nightscout/ is reserved (purpose, build, migration-group). Labels never decide what is therapy data; provenance does.

Namespace, extension. An extension is controller-specific typed data under a reverse-DNS namespace. Namespaces are first to claim per tenant and belong to the product across all its definitions. A namespace string proves nothing about authorship.

wellKnownRef. A definition's reference to a kind in the hub's well-known catalogue, instead of a copy of it.

Read selection, pin. Which version of an element a view shows: the operator's capabilities, then the owner's pin, then the version the live device source runs, then the newest stored.

Projected view, carrierView. A read-only document in the carrier's shape that the hub serves to older readers from a typed record, labelled projectedFrom. carrierView: served says the hub serves one for an element. A write to a projected document is refused projected-read-only.

dualWriteLink. For an element whose view is not served: the controller writes typed and carrier, linked by (instance id, the controller's record id), so counting and de-duplication follow the link.

Retention. A definition is kept while any stored record references it, any live instance runs it, or it is the product's current registration.

docs.title: L3 State and intent
docs.text:
Specified in the state and intent specification.

Intent kind, stateSpans entry. One kind of state a controller exposes (an override, a temporary target, a loop mode). It declares its slot, states, end reasons, carrier, where the request and the applied effect are recorded, initiators, definitions and what it accepts from the hub. State and intent S2.

Slot. The exclusivity group a kind occupies. Kinds in one slot exclude each other; a kind may declare which other slots coexist with it.

Channel. What roles are held on. For a kind with a slot, the channel is that slot. A slot is shared across products only through the hub's shared slot list or a declared sameAs; otherwise it is the product's own channel, <vendor>/<product>/<slot>. Other elements' channels are <vendor>/<product>/<element id>. REG §9.

Shared slot list, sameAs. specs/sync/shared-slots.yaml (override, loopMode, temporaryTarget). A kind declares sameAs: <shared slot> to join that channel. Two slots are never joined because their names look alike. REG §9.

Requested, applied. What was asked for, and what the controller reports it put into effect. They are recorded separately; a request is not evidence that anything happened.

End reason. Why a span ended: expired, cancelled, superseded, deleted before start, ended by trigger, or other with the controller's term.

Initiator. Who or what started an intent, in the controller's own vocabulary (Loop EnactTrigger, Trio AdjustmentSource, AndroidAPS Sources). A value outside the shared list is {value: other, controllerTerm}.

State version. sha256: over a product's active intents at a time, as the hub recorded them. A proposal names the version it was based on, and an approval is refused when it changed. It covers intents, not doses or carbs. State and intent A12.

Composition. How overlapping intents combine. Recorded as the controller reports it (reportedBy: controller, hubComputes: false); the hub never computes it.

StateSpan. Nocturne's span record (category, state, start, end, source, supersession), the container the series uses for observed state over time.

docs.title: L4 Change and sync
docs.text:
Write step. The single function every write path (v1, v3, socket, in-process) would call, deciding _id form, target, outcome (insert, merge, replace, unchanged, refused), server dates and one change event. WC §2.

Re-send rule. A re-send that matches a stored record stores no second copy and is answered with the stored ids. A differing re-send merges into the match (JSON Merge Patch: a null removes the field, as on an API v3 PATCH and a socket dbUpdate; a create or a replace stores a null as sent); an explicit update replaces. An identical re-send is rewritten on API v1, v3 and in-process and answered unchanged on the socket and for devicestatus (decided 2026-10-12, WC §6.1). Match order: identity §3.

Etag, precondition. sha256: over the canonical JSON of a resource's content, state and binding. Creates send If-None-Match: *; updates send If-Match. A missing precondition is 428 and a stale one is 412.

Load refusal, definite refusal. A typed write answered 429 or any 5xx is retried with backoff and never re-sent as its carrier. Any other refusal sends that record as its carrier at once. REG §6.

Cursor, watermark. An opaque server position from which changes are read. API v3 has lastModified and per-collection history/{from}; the proposed sync envelope reads every registered collection from one cursor. HS §3.2.

Storage socket. The API v3 socket that pushes stored changes to subscribed clients. Measured on dev 43289dde, only API v3 writes reach it (WC §3 U7).

quirksApplied, slotMapping. What the hub records on a reply and on the stored record when it applied a quirk mapping or decided a channel by sameAs, so a mapped value is never silent.

docs.title: L5 Authority
docs.text:
Specified in the authority specification.

Binding (boundTo), credential kind. The subject (or, in single mode, the shared secret) a product or instance is bound to; only it may update or retire it. credentialKind records whether a subject token or API_SECRET last wrote it. authority §3.

Owner, owner actions. The tenant owner, acting on ns-tenant-admin (or with API_SECRET in single mode). The owner may retire, block, unblock, release, transfer, free namespaces, transfer a role and pin a version, and never edits a registration's content.

Role. {channel, role, provenance} on an instance. source writes the channel's typed records as their source of record; command-sink accepts hub-originated commands for it; other roles are {value: other, controllerTerm}. Among live device instances each (channel, role) has one holder.

Provenance. device or simulated, per role. Only device-provenance data is therapy data in default views and exports, and a simulated command sink never receives a routed command.

Command destination. The live device instance holding command-sink on a channel. With no holder the command is refused no-command-destination; the hub never guesses (commands §2).

Command record, outcome. Proposed. The hub stores a command before it sends it, with the hash of its payload; only the destination reports the outcome, and fetched is never success (commands §4–§5).

Fetch-now signal, fetch bound. Proposed. A fetch-now signal tells one controller instance, on the socket or by a platform push, that something waits for its fetch; it carries nothing of the command. The fetch bound is the longest the instance goes between fetches: one cycle, or the shorter interval it declares (commands §7).

Plan, occurrence, mirror. Proposed. A plan is a recurring intent with elements, a trigger, bounds and an end date, proposed and approved in parts, then held and run by the controller; an occurrence is one time it runs, confirmed, approved, skipped or reported by the controller; the mirror is the hub's read-only record of the plan and its occurrences: what the controller reports, and the skips and ends the hub was asked for (plans).

Delegation, proposal. A delegation would let a principal grant a caregiver, app or agent a scoped, expiring, revocable authority; it is not specified. A proposal records an intended change for approval without authority to execute it; an approval by someone who may send the command turns it into one, and names the hash of one payload (proposed, commands §6). What a delegation design must provide is in configuration and delegation §5.4.

docs.title: L0 Identity: how records, definitions, instances and subjects are named
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-26 at 38fb13008.

Contributor-facing. Living specification, current at 2026-10-26 (cgm-remote-monitor dev 47723cda). Layer L0 of the platform index; terms are in the glossary. Status: specified, not implemented; §6, today's behaviour, is evidenced. Decisions: D20, the write contract's §6.1 and the 16.0.0 decisions (I2 on API v3, BF-170; the null rule of §3, Q1b). Queue: SPEC-ID.

Specification 1 of 8 in the reading order; every other specification uses these ids. Expect rules I1–I9, the contract ids, the match order per collection, the identifier format, today's behaviour in cgm-remote-monitor, and the conformance cases.

This page defines how records, definitions, instances and subjects are identified, and how a hub decides that a write is a re-send of something it already stores. Every other layer uses these ids; none of them redefines one.

docs.title: 1. Rules
docs.text:
# rule I1 Two ids, two jobs. identifier is the sync identity the client assigns: stable across retries and across the devices that write the same record. _id is the storage key the hub assigns. In the typed API, identifier is the controller's record id. I2 _id is 24 hex on every legacy surface. The hub assigns a 24-hex _id, on MongoDB and PostgreSQL alike; API v1 serves it, and API v3 reads do not return it (§6). On API v1, a client _id that is 24 hex, in either case, or {"$oid": …}, is kept as that ObjectId in lower case, and a client _id that is any other string is never stored as _id; it is handled by the quirks registry (I9). On API v3, a client-supplied _id in the body of a create, PUT or PATCH is refused with HTTP 400, whatever its form, and no quirk applies: a v3 client names its records by identifier (maintainer, 2026-10-25; BF-170). A hub's own newer APIs may use other ids. I3 An assigned _id's time is the receipt time. The first four bytes of an ObjectId the hub assigns are when the hub received the write, not the record's own time. Readers take a record's time from created_at or date. I4 Every write reply returns both ids. Per item: identifier (null when the client sent none and the path assigns none), _id, and matchedBy: identifier, _id, or null for a new record. On v1 and v3 this is the write step's WriteResult.items[]; on a typed write it is write.ids. A duplicate is never answered with a 5xx, an error to the callback or an empty acknowledgement. I5 A re-send matches on identifier first, then on _id, then on the collection's natural key (§3). A matched re-send stores no second copy and is answered with the stored ids, so a client needs no cache of server ids. I6 One identifier names one record per collection, for as long as the record is stored, and is compared exactly: case-sensitive, with no trimming or normalisation. For devicestatus, a re-send whose identifier is already stored writes nothing (no merge, no new record, no srvModified change) and is answered with the stored _id, on API v1 and v3 alike (maintainer, 2026-10-26; §3). I7 A typed re-send matches across instances of one product. A typed write matches a stored typed record of the same (vendor, product) with the same identifier, whichever instance sent it. The dual-write link (§2) is the exception: it is scoped by instance. I8 Projected documents have both ids. When a hub serves a typed record to older readers as a projected document, it assigns an ObjectId at the typed write and stores it with the record, so every read of that projection carries the same _id. The projection's identifier is the typed record's id. A write aimed at either id of a projected document is refused projected-read-only. I9 Today's _id handling is a recorded quirk. A non-ObjectId string _id on a treatment or entry is moved to identifier when UUID_HANDLING is on (the default) and the client sent no identifier, and dropped otherwise (QUIRK-TREATMENTS-006, QUIRK-ENTRIES-004). The hub records the move on the reply and the stored record as quirksApplied (moved-to-identifier or dropped).

identifier is the record's semantic identity in the data model (this CGM reading, this pump event, this carb entry), so two uploads of the same real thing carry the same value whichever app sends it; _id identifies the stored record (maintainer, 2026-10-18).

Rules I1–I9 are D20 rules 5–8 with the walk-through rows 1–3, specified in the hub-sync design §3.7, and the write contract's U1 and U6.

docs.title: 2. Contract ids
docs.text:
id form assigned by identifies definition id sha256: + the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the definition as submitted the hub computes it; the controller may compute it to check one immutable definition; equal content gives an equal id registration etag sha256: over the canonical JSON of {registration, state, boundTo} the hub one state of a product resource instance id a random lowercase UUID v4, generated once per running copy; any other form is refused invalid-instance-id the controller one running copy of a controller instance etag sha256: over the canonical JSON of {instance, boundTo, granted}; the lease is outside it the hub one state of an instance subject an opaque id of the principal a credential belongs to the credential issuer a principal; tokens rotate, the subject does not dual-write link (instance id, the controller's record id) the controller one typed record and its carrier copy

An instance id is never derived from a device name, model, serial number or the free-text devicestatus.device. A hub cannot check that an id is random; the contract states it. Bindings are to a subject, never to a token. These are specified in the registration specification §7–§8.

docs.title: 3. Match order per collection
docs.text:
The write step (write contract §2.2) resolves a re-send's target by trying keys in order; the first that resolves wins.

collection keys, in order on a match treatments identifier, _id, client identity, created_at + eventType merge entries identifier, _id, date + type merge devicestatus identifier, _id, NSCLIENT_ID, created_at + device for an identical body only an identifier match is unchanged whatever the body: nothing is written, no srvModified changes, and the reply carries the stored _id; on the other keys an identical body is unchanged and a differing body is a new record profile identifier, _id, NSCLIENT_ID, created_at merge food identifier, _id merge activity _id merge
  • Merge follows JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386): a field sent as null is removed from the stored record. The rule is recursive (a null inside a nested object removes that nested field) and an array is replaced whole, never merged element by element. It applies to a merge on match (a re-send that matches a stored record, in the collections above whose outcome is merge), to an API v3 PATCH, and to the socket's dbUpdate, which follows PATCH. It never applies to a replace (v1 PUT, v3 PUT), which stores the document as sent, or to any create, which stores a null as sent. On API v1 it runs after prepareData, so a field that prepareData removes or rewrites never reaches it. The socket's dbUpdateUnset stays as the explicit removal of named fields (maintainer, 2026-10-26; write contract Q1b; ships in 16.0.0).
  • Because the merge is recursive, a profile re-send whose store leaves out a named profile keeps that stored profile; removing it takes store: {"<name>": null} or a replace (PUT, which the profile editor uses). The same nested merge applies to an API v3 PATCH and a socket dbUpdate (maintainer, 2026-10-26, accepted with this consequence).
  • Client identity is treatment-fallback-key's client ids, with its rule that a write without identity matches only a stored record without identity.
  • The devicestatus natural key matches identical retries only, because Loop writes distinct statuses that share created_at and device (3,078 groups, 14,757 documents, at 11 of 12 corpus sites, measured 2026-10-12).
  • An _id matches every stored form of that id. A soft-deleted record is not a target for a create, so a re-send of a deleted record is stored again.

docs.title: 4. The identifier format
docs.text:
identifier is an opaque string, with one rule for every collection. Values follow the identifier conventions table, one row per record kind, in URL syntax: a source scheme for things that exist outside the app, the manufacturer as the scheme and the model as the first segment (dexcom://g7/<serial>/<offset>), and an app scheme for records made in an app (loop://carbs/<uuid>) (maintainer, 2026-10-18). What makes two devices agree is that they derive the id from the same inputs, not its format. A UUID is not required.

The constraints proposed for ID-FORMAT-DECISION, each grounded in the identifier format research §0:

# constraint C1 a JSON string with at least one non-whitespace character C2 at most 256 characters C3 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ : /; in an API v3 path the identifier is percent-encoded as one segment (an encoded / works on every v3 by-identifier route at 15.0.8 and fade2299, a raw / is 404: format research §3.4) C4 not exactly 24 hex characters, unless it equals the record's own _id C5 not history, . or .., and not a client placeholder such as invalid, undefined, null or NaN C6 one identifier, one record (I6) C7 compared exactly (I6)

A client that sends no usable identifier sends none, and the natural key applies. A client that uses today's v1 by-_id routes needs a UUID (§6).

docs.title: 5. Open decisions
docs.text: item question where the rules above stand ID-FORMAT-DECISION adopt C1–C7? opaque values, URL syntax and the source and app schemes are decided (maintainer, 2026-10-18); C1–C7 are proposed; I6 holds either way ID-CLIENT-OID-DECISION may a client create its own ObjectId as _id over API v1? the API v3 half is decided: I2 refuses a client _id on v3 (maintainer, 2026-10-25, BF-170). When identifier and _id match different records, identifier decides (maintainer, 2026-10-18), as I5 orders it. Open: whether the v1 half of the Loop reply's simple contract (a client-created ObjectId as _id) is recommended, which waits on Loop's answer and is carried by ID-SIMPLE-MATCH ID-V3-IMMUTABLE-DECISION on an identifier match, may date, device or eventType change? API v3 refuses it (400, reproduced by LOOP-ID-V3-IMMUTABLE); v1 does not ID-ABSENT-DECISION a write with no identifier: keep the time-key fallback, deprecate it, or require identifier? decided (maintainer, 2026-10-18): identifier becomes mandatory at a future version boundary and for registered controller instances; until then legacy paths keep the time-key fallback. Open: which version, and how a hub recognises a registered instance's write. Today v1 entries and treatments fall back to a time key, API v3 to its fallback fields; v1 device status has no key; two distinct doses with one created_at and eventType and no identifier are merged by §3 (UCA-SYNC-STORE-007) ID-DELETE-REUSE-DECISION after a delete, does a re-send of the same identifier resurrect, get refused, or create new? §3 stores it again today; a resurrected dose is UCA-SYNC-STORE-003 in the control-loop analysis API v3 resurrects a soft-deleted record on POST (measured 2026-10-18, record identity reference) ID-SCOPE-DECISION is identifier unique per collection, across collections, and per tenant? per collection today (each collection is its own MongoDB collection and index); the rules above do not say D20 choice 6 (text) is identifier null in the reply when the client sent none and the path assigns none? I4 states null, pending confirmation D20 choice 7 does a typed re-send match across instances of one product? I7 states yes, pending confirmation

docs.title: 6. Today, in cgm-remote-monitor
docs.text:
Read-derived unless marked, at official/dev fade2299 except where another revision is named. Measured per collection and path at 15.0.8 and fade2299 in the record identity reference (2026-10-18).

  • API v1 treatments match a re-send on identifier, and drop a client _id when identifier is present (lib/server/treatments.js:356-362 at 15.0.8).
  • API v1 entries and devicestatus do not match on identifier. Queue item ID-SIMPLE-MATCH adds that, after 15.0.9.
  • API v1 by-id routes treat only UUID-shaped values as identifiers (UUID_RE, lib/server/query.js:12). Stored identifiers are compared exactly, so an upper-case UUID matches only itself.
  • API v3 keeps a client identifier. When none is sent it computes a UUID v5 over the device, date and, for treatments, eventType (lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js:6, :106). It refuses a re-send whose date, device or eventType differs (400, reproduced).
  • API v3 and a body _id (dev 47723cda, since #8845): create, PUT and PATCH refuse a client-supplied _id with 400 (lib/api3/shared/operationTools.js:197-203, read), as I2 states. On v15.0.9 a 24-hex body _id is stored as a string (BF-170, reproduced). v3 reads do not return _id (lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/utils.js:10-16, read).
  • A devicestatus re-send with a stored identifier (dev 47723cda): API v1 stores a second record (no identifier match) and API v3 replaces the stored record and moves its srvModified (reproduced, the devicestatus study of 2026-10-26). I6's rule is built for 16.0.0 with ID-SIMPLE-MATCH on branch bf/16.0.0-null-removes.
  • A null in an update (dev 47723cda): a merge on match stores a field sent as null as null ($set), on every path, and tests/api.profiles.resend.test.js:218 pins that. §3's removal is built for 16.0.0 on branch bf/16.0.0-null-removes (in progress), with BF-195's fix.
  • UUID_HANDLING (default on) moves a non-24-hex string _id to identifier on treatments and entries, as I9 describes (lib/server/treatments.js:394-411, lib/server/entries.js:267-284 at official a8888f0d).
  • The write paths disagree. A record created through one path and re-sent without _id through another is stored twice in 38 of 66 ordered path pairs (measured on dev 43289dde; write contract §0). The write step (WRITE-CONTRACT) is what makes §3 hold on every path.

What controllers send is in the client id analyses, the identifier format research §1, and the quirks registry: QUIRK-TREATMENTS-006 (Loop override _id), QUIRK-ENTRIES-004 and QUIRK-TREATMENTS-007 (Trio's id member).

20 cases, under specs/sync/conformance/. Checked by tools/nsschema/test_registration_quirks.py and tools/nsschema/test_registration_instances.py; the reference functions check the cases, they are not a hub.

case rule quirks/carrier-write-both-ids I4 quirks/carrier-hex-id-kept I2 quirks/carrier-resend-matches-objectid I2, I5 quirks/carrier-resend-identifier-first I5 quirks/carrier-resend-matches-identifier I5 quirks/carrier-uuid-id-moved I9 quirks/carrier-uuid-id-dropped I9 quirks/carrier-uuid-entries-moved I9 quirks/carrier-uuid-resend-matches I5, I9 quirks/typed-write-assigns-objectid I2, I3 quirks/typed-write-resend-same-ids I5 quirks/write-projected-read-only-by-objectid I8 quirks/write-stored-carrier-by-objectid I8 (control) instances/project-served I8 instances/write-projected-read-only I8 instances/write-stored-carrier I8 (control) instances/instance-invalid-id §2 instance id instances/definition-id-mismatch §2 definition id instances/dual-write-linked §2 dual-write link instances/dual-write-not-linked-across-instances §2 dual-write link

Not covered by a case: I2's API v3 refusal (the carrier cases do not name an API version); I7 across two instances (typed-write-resend-same-ids re-sends from one instance); §3's per-collection keys, which the write contract's gates measure against cgm-remote-monitor rather than a reference function; and §4's format, until it is decided.

docs.title: L3 and L5 Plans: how a plan is proposed, approved in parts, held by the controller and mirrored by the hub
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 127f69e16.

Contributor-facing. Living specification, current at main b081a15c (2026-10-18). Layers L3 and L5 of the platform index; terms are in the glossary. Decisions: D18 and D19 and the maintainer's answers of 2026-10-18 recorded in the command queue and planning note. Queue: SPEC-PLANS.

Specification 6 of 8 in the reading order; after commands, whose proposals, approvals, commands and outcomes it builds on, and before sync-transport. Expect what a plan is, rules PN1–PN18 for the plan object, its approval, the controller's hold and the hub's mirror, occurrences and ending, compatibility, open items, and the conformance cases.

A plan is a recurring intent with its trigger, bounds and end date, approved once and run by the controller: eating soon before a weekday lunch, a temporary target before a calendar's exercise, a week of school overrides. It moves a decision from the moment to the morning or the week. The controller holds and runs the plan; the hub records the proposal, the approval and what the controller reports, and keeps a read-only mirror of the plan and its occurrences. The hub never schedules an occurrence, never decides whether one runs, and never doses (D18).

Status: proposed and specified with cases; none is implemented. The risk classes, floors and windows follow evidence-weighted approval, a draft that needs review by a qualified clinician before any of it is relied on.

docs.title: 1. Files
docs.text: file holds tools/nsschema/plans.py the reference decision function, built on commands.py tools/nsschema/test_plans.py checks every case and the invariants in §10 specs/sync/conformance/plans/ hand-authored cases and FORMAT.md commands proposals (CM11–CM16, CM22), commands and outcomes (CM1–CM10, CM21, CM23–CM25) that plans use evidence-weighted approval risk classes R0–R6, floors FL1–FL8, the approval paths

docs.title: 2. What a plan is
docs.text:
A plan has four levels of decision, and each has its own party and its own check:

level horizon who acts what it does here policy days to weeks a proposer (often an agent), reviewers, the person or a delegate proposes, reviews and approves the plan, in parts (§4) confirmation hours the proposer under the plan's grant; the person confirms, approves, skips one occurrence (§6) moment minutes the person, a caregiver ordinary commands (commands §4) algorithm five minutes the controller runs each occurrence within its bounds after its own checks

One controller instance, the destination, holds the plan and is the only thing that acts on the pump. Agents, reviewers, a delegate and the person all work on the same plan record.

A plan's life, for a weekday lunch with an eating-soon target that runs on the plan's approval and a meal bolus approved each day:

sequenceDiagram
  accTitle: A plan's life
  accDescr: An agent proposes a plan with a standing eating-soon element and a per-occurrence meal bolus. A reviewer attaches an independent review, and the person approves both elements by id and hash. The hub records one command and a read-only mirror; the controller validates and holds the plan, and its report makes the mirror active. Each morning the agent confirms the day's occurrence; the person approves the day's meal bolus within 12 hours before it. The controller runs the occurrence after its own checks and reports it. The person can skip a day or end the plan at any time, and the hub cancels what was queued for it.
  participant G as Agent (proposer)
  participant V as Reviewer
  participant P as Person or delegate
  participant H as Hub (mirror)
  participant C as Controller
  G->>H: propose plan: eating soon (standing), meal bolus (per occurrence) (PN1-PN4)
  V->>H: review (PN6)
  P->>H: approve elements by id and hash (PN5-PN7)
  H->>C: one command with the accepted elements (PN8)
  C->>H: holds it: succeeded (PN9), mirror active
  loop each weekday
    G->>H: confirm the day's occurrence (PN12)
    H->>C: confirmation
    P->>H: approve the day's meal bolus, within 12 h before (PN13)
    H->>C: occurrence approval
    Note over C: bounds, doses since, withdrawal criteria<br/>with fresh data (PN10), runs once (PN17)
    C->>H: occurrence ran, withdrawn or refused (PN11)
  end
  opt skip a day or end the plan (PN14, PN16)
    P->>H: skip or end
    H->>C: skip or end, and queued occurrence commands cancelled
  end
  C->>H: ended at endsAt (PN15)

docs.title: 3. The plan object (proposed)
docs.text: # rule PN1 A plan is a proposal. A plan is proposed as a proposal (CM11, CM12) whose kind is plan, which names its product (422 product-required) and whose payload has elements, a trigger, startsAt, endsAt and requiredReviews. It is routed when made (commands §2) on the channel the product declares for plans, and the destination's definitionId is recorded. Its own open time is bounded by the operator's plans.maxProposalSeconds, not by commands.maxExpirySeconds, so a plan proposed for review at a visit weeks away can stay open; beyond it the proposal is refused 422 expiry-too-long, as CM3 refuses a command. PN2 Elements. Each element has an id unique in the plan, a kind (PN3 says how an undeclared kind is classed), the channel it acts on, its content and its path: standing (runs on the plan's approval) or per-occurrence (each occurrence needs its own approval, §6). Each element's hash is sha256: over the canonical JSON of the element (CM1's rule), and the proposal's payloadHash covers the whole plan. PN3 Risk class comes from the definition. The destination's definition declares a risk class per element kind, R0 (inform) to R6 (safety limits), as evidence-weighted approval §2 defines them. A kind with no declared class is R4. The hub reads the class; it never derives one from the content (CM5). PN4 Structural floors at proposal. After the proposer's checks (CM12) and before routing, a proposal is refused 422, with nothing recorded, when: an element id repeats or there are none (invalid-plan); an element is R6 (local-only); an R5 element is standing (standing-not-allowed); an R3 or R4 element is standing without standingConditions naming at least one withdrawal criterion, each with its signal and evaluatedBy (controller or agent), the mitigation reduced-portion, and a companion element of the plan, the eating-soon target the reduced portion goes with (standing-conditions-required); a standing R3 element is in a plan with no standing R4 element (standing-carbs-without-insulin, FL2); endsAt is missing or not after startsAt (ends-required); or endsAt is more than the operator's plans.maxPlanSeconds after startsAt (plan-too-long). The hub checks that the conditions are declared; the controller checks that they hold (PN10). FL1's other choice, a human approval of each occurrence within the 12 hours before, is the per-occurrence path (PN13), so a standing insulin element always carries the reduced portion. After routing, an element whose channel has a command-sink holder other than the destination is 409 element-destination-differs: the plan's elements act through the one controller that holds the plan.

docs.title: 4. Approving a plan (proposed)
docs.text: # rule PN5 An approval accepts elements. An approval of a plan names each accepted element by id and hash. An approval that accepts nothing is 422 nothing-accepted; an id the plan does not have is 422 unknown-element; a hash that differs from the element's is 409 hash-mismatch. The elements not named are recorded as declined. An approval closes the proposal: accepting a declined element later is a new proposal. PN6 Who approves, and what must be attached first. CM14 applies: an agent's proposal is never approved by the subject that proposed it. An approval that accepts an R3 or higher element comes from the subject marked as the person or a delegate acting for them (FL5), never from an agent's credential, else 403 not-person-or-delegate. A review counts when an evaluation (CM16) names it and comes from a subject other than the proposer. Each review named in requiredReviews must have been attached, and a plan that accepts an R3 or higher element needs at least one review whatever requiredReviews says (the framework's reviews-then-approve path); else 409 review-required. Whether two agents run by one operator are independent of each other is open (§9). PN7 What the approval checks. In this order: the approver (CM14 and PN6, 403); nothing-accepted and unknown-element (422); PN4's floors over the accepted elements alone (422), so an approval that keeps standing carbs while declining the standing insulin is standing-carbs-without-insulin, and one that accepts standing insulin without its companion is companion-declined; the proposal's state (CM13: proposal-expired, proposal-closed); hash-mismatch (PN5); the reviews (PN6); routing again, 409 destination-changed when the holder changed (CM13); 409 definition-changed when the destination's definitionId differs from the one recorded at the proposal; and 409 state-changed when the state version of any accepted element's channel differs from the plan's basedOn for that channel; a channel missing from basedOn differs unless the channel has no state version. basedOn for a plan is a map from channel to the channel's state version, the part of A12 on that channel, so an unrelated override does not stale a plan. CM22's doses check does not apply to a plan; doses are checked at each occurrence by the controller (PN10). PN8 An accepted plan becomes one command. The command's payload is the plan with only the accepted elements, and its payloadHash is the hash of that payload, which the controller checks (CM10) and decides once (CM21). As CM13 says of any approval, the command carries the plan's proposalId. It expires at endsAt or commands.maxExpirySeconds after the approval, whichever is sooner. The hub records the plan's mirror (PN11) in state approved, with the accepted and declined elements. The replies to plan operations (PN8, PN12–PN14, PN16) do not carry CM24's outstanding list; the mirror shows the plan's occurrences, and PN18 lists them on each element's channel.

docs.title: 5. The controller holds the plan; the hub mirrors it (proposed)
docs.text:
# rule PN9 The controller decides whether to hold it. On the plan's command the controller validates the plan against its own limits and definitions, and reports succeeded when it holds the plan, or refused or failed with a reason (CM7, CM8). The mirror becomes active, or refused for either refusal, from that report. A plan command handed over and then unconfirmed (CM3) leaves the mirror approved, because the controller may hold the plan. PN10 The controller runs each occurrence. At each occurrence the controller applies its own checks: the bounds of each element, the doses and carbs since (CM23), the plan's withdrawal criteria with data it judges fresh, and, for a standing R3 or R4 element, the declared mitigation. An occurrence whose criteria cannot be evaluated with fresh data does not run. The hub schedules nothing and sends nothing at an occurrence's time. PN11 The mirror. The hub keeps, per plan, its state (approved, active, refused, ending, ended), its accepted and declined elements, and its occurrences, each keyed by the controller's occurrence key with a state: confirmed, approved, skip-requested (set by the hub, §6), and ran, withdrawn, skipped, refused, missed (reported by the controller, with a reason where one applies, and for ran the identity of the intent or record that shows it). The states the controller owns move only on its reports; the hub sets only what it was asked (skip-requested, ending). Only the destination's bound subject reports (CM7: anyone else is 403 not-registration-owner). A report on a plan the controller may hold (approved, active, ending) is accepted, and on an approved plan it also shows the controller holds it, so the mirror becomes active; on a plan that is refused or ended it is 409 plan-not-active. Anyone who may read the outstanding list (CM24) may read the mirror, which lists occurrences even when there are none; anyone else is 403 not-authorised.

The mirror's states. Each state the controller owns moves only on its reports; the hub sets ending when it is asked to end the plan.

stateDiagram-v2
  accTitle: Plan mirror states
  accDescr: An approved plan's mirror becomes active when the controller reports holding it, or refused when the controller refuses or fails the plan command. The person, the approver or the proposer can end a plan that is approved, active or ending; ending again re-sends the end. The mirror becomes ended when the controller reports the end, either after an end request or at endsAt.
  [*] --> approved: approval accepted (PN8)
  approved --> active: controller holds it (PN9, PN11)
  approved --> refused: refused or failed (PN9)
  approved --> ending: end requested (PN16)
  active --> ending: end requested (PN16)
  ending --> ending: end sent again (PN16)
  active --> ended: reported at endsAt (PN15)
  ending --> ended: reported (PN16)
  refused --> [*]
  ended --> [*]

docs.title: 6. Occurrences (proposed)
docs.text:
# rule PN12 The plan is its proposer's grant to confirm. While the mirror is active and before endsAt, the plan's proposer, from its proposing instance, may confirm an occurrence: the hub records it and sends the controller a command naming the plan and the occurrence, expiring at the occurrence's time. A confirmation is evidence that the occasion is happening; it never releases a dose by itself (FL5), and the controller still applies PN10. The checks, in order: another subject or instance is 403 outside-grant; a proposer that no longer holds api:proposals:create or its propose role on the plan channel (CM12) is 403 role-not-granted; a plan that is not active is 409 plan-not-active; at or past endsAt, 409 plan-ended; an occurrence time outside startsAt to endsAt is 409 occurrence-outside-plan; more than plans.maxAdvanceApprovalSeconds ahead, 409 too-early; at or after the occurrence time, 409 occurrence-passed; and an occurrence that is skip-requested or reported finished (ran, withdrawn, skipped, refused, missed) is 409 occurrence-closed. PN13 A per-occurrence element needs an approval per occurrence. A per-occurrence element runs only on an approval of that occurrence, which names the plan, the occurrence key, its time, the element and its hash. The approver holds api:commands:create (403 not-authorised) and follows CM14; an R3 or higher element is approved by the person or a delegate (403 not-person-or-delegate), and an R5 element by the person (403 person-required, FL3). Then, in order: the plan is active and before endsAt (PN12's 409s); the element is per-occurrence and accepted, else 409 not-per-occurrence; its hash, else 409 hash-mismatch; and PN12's occurrence checks, so the approval is accepted from exactly plans.maxAdvanceApprovalSeconds before the occurrence (12 hours, pending clinical review) until the occurrence's time, on an occurrence not closed. An accepted approval sends the controller a command for that occurrence and element, expiring at the occurrence's time, as a confirmation's does. PN14 Skipping an occurrence. The person (CM14), the plan's approver, or its proposer from its proposing instance (an agent whose live data contradicts the occasion withdraws it this way) may skip an occurrence while the plan is approved or active and before endsAt; anyone else is 403 not-authorised, a plan in another state 409 plan-not-active, at or past endsAt 409 plan-ended, and an occurrence already closed 409 occurrence-closed. The hub sets it skip-requested, cancels the occurrence's queued confirmation and approval commands as CM25 does (final before hand-over, a request after), and sends the controller a skip command expiring commands.maxExpirySeconds after the request; the controller reports skipped, or ran if it had already run.

An occurrence's states. The hub records confirmed, approved and skip-requested as it is asked; the controller reports how the occurrence finished, and a finished occurrence takes no further confirmation or approval.

stateDiagram-v2
  accTitle: Occurrence states
  accDescr: An occurrence is confirmed by the proposer or approved by the person or a delegate, in either order, or skipped. A skip cancels what was queued for the occurrence. The controller reports how it finished: ran, withdrawn, skipped, refused or missed; a skip request ends as skipped, or ran if the controller had already run it. A finished occurrence is closed.
  state "skip-requested" as skip
  state "finished, reported by the controller" as finished {
    ran
    withdrawn
    skipped
    refused
    missed
  }
  state open {
    [*] --> confirmed: proposer confirms (PN12)
    [*] --> approved: person or delegate approves (PN13)
    confirmed --> approved: approved (PN13)
  }
  [*] --> open
  [*] --> skip: skipped (PN14)
  open --> skip: skipped (PN14)
  open --> finished: controller reports (PN11)
  skip --> finished: skipped, or ran if it already had (PN14)
  finished --> [*]: closed (PN12)

docs.title: 7. Ending a plan (proposed)
docs.text: # rule PN15 The controller ends a plan at endsAt. It reports ended, and no occurrence runs after endsAt. The hub never extends a plan; a longer plan is a new proposal. PN16 The person can end a plan at any time. The person, the plan's approver, or its proposer from its proposing instance may end a plan the controller may hold (approved, active or ending): the mirror becomes ending, the plan's queued occurrence commands are cancelled as CM25 cancels, and the controller receives an end command expiring commands.maxExpirySeconds after the request, then reports ended. Ending a plan that is already ending sends the end command again, for an end that was lost. An end command is never cancelled (409 not-cancellable). A plan that is refused or ended is 409 plan-not-active; anyone else is 403 not-authorised. A confirmation or an occurrence approval for a plan that is ending or ended is 409 plan-not-active. PN17 An occurrence runs once. The controller runs each occurrence key at most once, whatever confirmations and approvals arrive for it (CM21), and reports one finished state for it. PN18 Occurrence commands are listed where they act. CM24's outstanding list for a channel includes each queued occurrence command of a plan with an accepted element on that channel, as well as the plan channel's own commands, so a caregiver looking at the bolus channel sees a plan's pending bolus.

docs.title: 8. Compatibility
docs.text:
Per app: compatibility L3.

No released controller holds a plan from a hub. The nearest precedent runs on the controller: AndroidAPS's automation plugin (dev 7e1d537d49) triggers on recurring time, location, Wi-Fi network, steps and heart rate, and acts with a temporary target, a profile percentage, scenes, a notification or an SMS, and with no bolus or carb action. A plan under PN1–PN18 is the hub-side record of such a rule when it is proposed or approved away from the phone.

older hub newer hub older controller no plans the product declares no plan channel, so a plan proposal is refused at routing (commands §2) newer controller no plans member in the capability document: the controller keeps its rules local and sends no mirror reports PN1–PN18

docs.title: 9. Open
docs.text:
1. Values for clinical review: plans.maxAdvanceApprovalSeconds (12 hours), the risk class of each element kind, which withdrawal signals suffice and how fresh their data must be, and the reduced portion (evidence-weighted approval §9).
  2. The approval paths that depend on evidence (notify, cancel window) for R0–R2 occurrences: PN12 and PN13 cover confirmation and approval; the lighter paths wait for evidence classes on evaluations (CM16).
  3. The trigger grammar. PN1 names trigger; recurrence, local time and time zones, and conditions on location or activity are not specified, and the hub stores them unread.
  4. Where withdrawal criteria are evaluated when both the controller and an agent can, and whether both must agree.
  5. Approver signatures over the accepted elements, which let a controller detect a hub that built the wrong subset (partial acceptance).
  6. The plan channel a product declares, and the capability document member that says a hub serves plans.
  7. Independence of reviews: whether a review by a second agent run by the same person or operator counts toward PN6 (UCA-PLAN-010 in the control-loop analysis).
  8. Doses since, for an occurrence approval: CM24's list shows doses since the earliest outstanding item; whether an occurrence approval returns the doses since the previous occurrence.
  9. Required reviews per occurrence for R5 and for R3–R4 occurrences with weak evidence (FL3, the framework's reviews-then-approve path).
  10. Not specified: an adjusted plan replacing one the controller holds (journey PL3.3); several plans active on one channel at once; occurrence reports for elements not accepted or dated after endsAt; a maximum plan length per risk class, for clinical review; a field on an intent naming the plan and occurrence that started it (FB-PLAN-004).

docs.title: 10. Conformance cases
docs.text:
PN10 and PN17 have no case: they are the controller's, and the hub has nothing to refuse.

Checked by tools/nsschema/test_plans.py against tools/nsschema/plans.py, which also checks on every case that no command carries a declined element; each command was made at the time of the call that named it (the hub schedules nothing); every element a command carries is the proposed element, byte for byte, and a plan command's hash is the hash of what it carries; every accepted standing R3 or R4 element carries its withdrawal criteria, mitigation and an accepted companion, and standing carbs come with standing insulin; a plan or occurrence approval at R3 or higher comes from the person or a delegate, and at R5 from the person; occurrence operations happen only while the controller holds the plan; an occurrence approval falls inside its window and never comes from the agent that proposed the plan; and nothing is confirmed or approved for an occurrence after it was skipped.

docs.title: L1 Records: the typed observations a hub stores, and how today's documents decompose into them
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 13259e01d.

Contributor-facing. Living specification, current at main 92a7d31b (2026-10-18). Layer L1 of the platform index; terms are in the glossary; record ids are in the identity specification. Status: evidenced, not implemented: the catalogue is generated from a shipped typed model and the corpus. Decision: D11, for devicestatus; the rest of this page is proposed (§2). Queue: SPEC-RECORDS.

Specification 2 of 8 in the reading order; after identity, before registration, which declares what these records mean. Expect rules R1–R9, the generated catalogue of primitives and their evidence grades, decomposition, settings snapshots, and named test checks.

A controller sends what it has, in the shape it has it: a treatment, a device status, a profile. The hub keeps that document and also decomposes it into typed observation primitives, so queries stay bounded and a dose can be replayed against the inputs that produced it. This page says which primitives exist, how much evidence stands behind each field, how a composite document is decomposed, and what a settings snapshot must carry for a replay to be faithful.

docs.title: 1. Files
docs.text: file what it is specs/sync/primitives.yaml the observation catalogue, every field graded; generated by make schema-primitives (tools/nsschema/primitives.py) specs/sync/controller-settings.schema.json the effective-dated settings snapshot (§5) specs/nsschema/dosing-input-sources.yaml every dosing input each algorithm family declares, with where it is recorded specs/sync/sensitivity.yaml the two-axis sensitivity labels and the disclosure profiles (§6) specs/nsschema/*.model.json today's collections as stored, from the census specs/conformance/observability-profile.yaml the observability obligations a registration formalises

docs.title: 2. Rules
docs.text:
# rule R1 Composite on the wire, primitive in storage. The hub decomposes a written document into observation primitives and keeps the composite beside them, so "what did the device send" stays answerable and a legacy reader can be answered from the composite. A treatment carrying insulin and carbs becomes a Bolus and a CarbIntake sharing a correlation id; a device status becomes an ApsSnapshot, a PumpSnapshot and an UploaderSnapshot; a profile becomes TherapySettings and four schedules. R2 Decomposition is declared, not hard-coded. What a document decomposes into is declared by its registration: documents[].decomposesTo with a structural discriminator ({path: loop, test: is-object}), never the free-text device string (registration §3). The decomposition is data, so it does not become another list that drifts beside the API description, the indexes and the census model. R3 Decomposition sits above the storage seam. It runs for single-tenant and multi-tenant storage alike, as type coercion does. Only devicestatus's indexed fields become columns; its other nodes stay in the stored document, and the decomposed series are separate relations with their own schemas. R4 Every field carries an evidence grade. measured: a wire path in the corpus populates it, or the shipped decomposer maps it from a path the corpus carries. declared: a typed model declares it and the corpus shows no source. proposed: this programme asks for it and no shipped model has it. A grade is evidence, not endorsement; a replay or a consumer treats a declared field as unverified. R5 Settings are a snapshot, effective-dated and versioned with the build. A controller publishes a ControllerSettings snapshot on change, not per cycle, with effectiveFrom (and effectiveUntil when known) and the controller's product and version. A setting that changed mid-history invalidates a replay that assumed one value, and algorithm behaviour changes between releases. R6 Absent is not a default. Every setting is optional. A setting a controller does not publish is recorded as not published and never filled with a default value, because "not published" is information a replay needs. R7 Configuration and per-cycle state are separate. Settings hold configuration. Values a controller computes each cycle (the meal-detection slopes, flatBGsDetected, IOB components, the effective sensitivity and carb ratio) are not settings; their place is the cycle's record, and the scheduled forms belong to the schedule primitives. ApsSnapshot does not carry the meal-detection slopes or flatBGsDetected today (§3, fields no primitive carries). R8 Replay inputs are declared with their status. A registration lists every dosing input the controller could supply (replayInputs), with its status (recorded, partial, derivable, absent) and path; an input it has but does not publish has a null path. Completeness is then a published number per controller, not an estimate. A derived input is recomputed from stored history and is not the value the controller used; recorded and derivable are never reported as one figure. R9 Every field has a sensitivity label. A field is labelled on two axes, a level and a category (§6). In the label assignment that generates the schemas, an unlabelled field is identifying: a field is argued down, never silently up. In a registration, a declared field with no label falls under sensitivity.unlabelledPolicy, withhold when absent (registration G2).

Status. R2 and R3 are D11 for devicestatus, where D11 also says a known catalogue ships with Nightscout and a controller may publish or correct its own. Applying R1–R3 to every collection, and R4–R9, are proposed: the catalogue (0.1-draft), the settings schema and the sensitivity labels are drafts for the maintainer and the controller authors.

docs.title: 3. The catalogue
docs.text:
Sixteen primitives, each a typed class in Nocturne's V4 model. Generated from specs/sync/primitives.yaml.

primitive group typed by fields measured declared what it is SensorGlucose observation Nocturne V4 SensorGlucose.cs 14 8 6 A CGM reading. BGCheck observation Nocturne V4 BGCheck.cs 5 4 1 A fingerstick or meter reading. Bolus delivery Nocturne V4 Bolus.cs 13 6 7 A discrete insulin dose, manual or algorithm-initiated. TempBasal delivery Nocturne V4 TempBasal.cs 14 6 8 A temporary basal rate for a bounded interval. CarbIntake delivery Nocturne V4 CarbIntake.cs 5 2 3 A carbohydrate entry. ApsSnapshot decision Nocturne V4 ApsSnapshot.cs 25 23 2 One controller cycle: the state it saw and what it decided. The record a replay is checked against. PumpSnapshot device Nocturne V4 PumpSnapshot.cs 13 11 2 Pump state at a point in time. UploaderSnapshot device Nocturne V4 UploaderSnapshot.cs 6 4 2 The uploading device's own state. DeviceEvent device Nocturne V4 DeviceEvent.cs 2 2 0 A site change, sensor start, cartridge change. TherapySettings settings Nocturne V4 TherapySettings.cs 18 8 10 The therapy configuration in force. BasalSchedule settings Nocturne V4 BasalSchedule.cs 2 1 1 Scheduled basal rates by time of day. CarbRatioSchedule settings Nocturne V4 CarbRatioSchedule.cs 2 1 1 Carb ratio by time of day. SensitivitySchedule settings Nocturne V4 SensitivitySchedule.cs 2 1 1 Insulin sensitivity by time of day. Field matching against the corpus is by leaf name and by the decomposer's own assignments, read from its source (Iob = ds.OpenAps.Iob?.Iob). A measured grade that rests only on a generic leaf name is flagged low_confidence and still counted as measured; no field carries the flag in the catalogue as committed. The corpus was fetched through API v1, so fields only API v3 carries (identifier, srvCreated, srvModified) and the settings collection are not observable in it.

Where the evidence is weak. TherapySettings and the four schedules, because settings mostly do not reach the corpus; the schedules' entry interiors are unexamined. Anything about AndroidAPS: the corpus has no AndroidAPS closed-loop site.

Fields no primitive carries. Proposed, each a request to a controller's authors. "Input of" is the algorithm family whose dosing-input map names the input; Loop records the equivalents of three oref0 inputs (profile.maxBasal, profile.suspendThreshold, profile.dosingStrategy) under profile.loopSettings. The reason each is asked for is in specs/sync/primitives.yaml.
