docs.title: 4. Decomposition, measured
docs.text:
collection what is known source treatments Nocturne's routing places 99.86% of treatments by eventType alone and 0.13% by the data present. The 22 unroutable documents all carry Suspend Pump, Nightscout's documented spelling; Nocturne's V4 decomposition keys on Pump Suspend, the words reversed, so fixing that constant routes every treatment in the corpus. This measures which branch a document takes, not the records each branch writes. Five leaf field names have no typed home, among them userEnteredAt on 10 of 11 sites, so a named extension location is still needed hub-sync §3.3; extensibility models §3 devicestatus a typed model that reads only declared paths drops 56 of 166 observed paths, nine of them on 10 of 11 sites, because only the top level has an extension point; Loop's dose recommendation (bolusVolume on 26.1% of statuses, tempBasalAdjustment on 6.1%) and the majority pump shape (pump.bolusing, pump.suspended, 85.1%) are among them. Decomposition coverage is not measured devicestatus and profile fidelity §2 profile the typed model drops 1 of 66 observed paths; Loop's loopSettings subtree was undeclared in this repository's 2025.1.0 specs when measured (2026-09-10). Decomposition coverage is not measured same; typed schema evidence §4.4 entries the typed model drops 1 of 19 observed paths devicestatus and profile fidelity §2

Every loss above is a nested field. A composite document nested more than one level deep needs an extension point at each level, or decomposition into separately typed records; R1–R3 choose the second. The activity collection already works that way in production: xDrip+ posts {type: "hr-bpm", bpm} and {type: "steps-total", steps}, discriminated by type.

Not measured: whether a decomposed set recomposes into a document a legacy client accepts, which decides whether decomposition can sit behind the existing API.

docs.title: 5. Settings snapshot
docs.text:
ControllerSettings (controller-settings.schema.json) requires effectiveFrom, controller (product and version required; vendor and algorithmFamily optional) and settings; it allows effectiveUntil. It is written to the API v3 settings collection, so it needs no new endpoint. Its nineteen settings, with their status in the corpus:

status today settings recorded dia, maxBasalRate, maxBolus, units partial dosingStrategy, maxBasal, recommendationType, suspendThreshold derivable maxDailyBasal absent automaticBolusApplicationFactor, carbAbsorptionModel, gradualTransitionsThreshold, includePositiveVelocityAndRC, maxActiveInsulinMultiplier, maxIob, microBolusAllowed, recommendationInsulinModel, useIntegralRetrospectiveCorrection, useMidAbsorptionISF

Dosing safety limits reach Nightscout as settings from Loop, as profile.loopSettings.*; no oref0-family controller records maxIob there. An oref0 rig uploads its preferences, max_iob among them, with each device status (devicestatus.preferences; oref0 d219baf9 bin/ns-status.js:40-49,175-177): configuration repeated every cycle, not a snapshot published on change (R5). This is read from controller source together with the corpus: the corpus alone would credit Trio with limits it never writes, and every AndroidAPS statement on this page is read from source. A registration's settings.fields may name a setting or declare it typed, by typeRef to its ControllerSettings definition (registration G2).

Completeness. Of the dosing inputs each family declares, the share Nightscout records (hub-sync §4.2):

declared inputs recorded recorded or derivable Loop 20 20% 55% Trio and AndroidAPS (oref0 family) 40 50% 72%

These are source-derived estimates of what is recorded, not measured replay accuracy.

docs.title: 6. Sensitivity labels
docs.text:
specs/sync/sensitivity.yaml labels a field on two axes:

  • level:
  • secret: credential or key material; never leaves the party that needs it.
  • identifying: directly identifies a person, install or device; stripped, or replaced by a stable, non-reversible pseudonym.
  • quasi-identifying: narrowing in combination; coarsened where the analysis allows.
  • descriptive: a measurement, setting or vocabulary; still health data.
  • category: credential, identity, device, health-measurement, health-derived, therapy-setting, temporal, location, free-text, vocabulary.

A disclosure profile (full, clinical, replay, effect-only, research, schema-evidence) admits fields up to a level and within listed categories. The label assignments are derived from the redaction policy this repository applies and from the census. What may lawfully be disclosed under any profile needs qualified review.

docs.title: 7. Open
docs.text:
• Decomposition coverage of devicestatus and profile (§4), and round-tripping to legacy readers.
  • The ScheduleEntry interior of the four schedules.
  • Every AndroidAPS field, from data.
  • The proposed fields (§3), which only controller authors can publish (PROPOSAL-REG-CONTROLLERS).
  • ControllerSettings is open: its settings object allows any additional member, and it carries an untyped x-aid-extensions member. Controller-specific settings belong in typed registration extensions (registration G2).
  • make schema-primitives truncates a proposed field's reason at 160 characters and gives some partial inputs the reason "a dosing input no controller publishes".

docs.title: 8. Checks
docs.text:
10 checks, in tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py, run with python3 -m pytest -q tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py. The catalogue is regenerated with make schema-primitives; it reads the corpus, which is not in this repository.

check holds that tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_every_named_primitive_is_defined every primitive a registration's decomposesTo names is in the catalogue tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_catalogue_grades_every_field every field carries a grade (R4) tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_decomposer_assignments_are_read_from_source the decomposer parser finds Sgv behind Mgdl and Basal behind Entries, the assignments R4's grades read tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_treatments_route_to_their_primitive treatments route by eventType (§4) tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_suspend_pump_is_unroutable_which_is_the_finding the documented Suspend Pump does not route through V4's reversed constant, and Pump Suspend does (§4) tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_settings_schema_is_valid_and_accepts_a_partial_publication a partial settings snapshot validates (R6) tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_settings_schema_requires_a_build_version a snapshot needs the build version (R5) tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_per_cycle_state_is_kept_out_of_settings per-cycle state is not a setting (R7) tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_dosing_input_map_loads_and_is_well_formed the dosing-input map is well formed (R8) tools/nsschema/test_nsschema.py::test_completeness_is_reported_not_assumed Loop's recorded share is computed, strictly between 0 and 1, and its recorded-or-derivable share is no smaller (R8)

docs.title: L2 Registration: how a controller declares what its data means, and how a hub accepts it
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-26 at 36487a5dd.

Contributor-facing. Living specification, current at main 8d2b93ed (2026-10-18). Layer L2 of the platform index; terms are in the glossary; ids are defined in the identity specification. Status: specified, not implemented; the first hub implementation is HUB-REG-CRM. Decisions: D18 and its addendum, D19, D20 and the maintainer's decisions of 2026-10-14, 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-17 recorded there. Queue: SPEC-REGISTRATION.

Specification 3 of 8 in the reading order, and the largest; after records, before state and intent, which uses its grammar. Expect rules G1–G5 and Q1–Q4, the grammar, the capability document, products, definitions, instances, channels and roles, labels, typed writes, projected views, quirks, and the conformance cases.

A controller declares what its data means; the hub accepts the declaration element by element, stores typed records for what it accepts, and tells the controller to write everything else in today's document shapes. Several running copies of a controller can share a site without overwriting one another. The hub records what each copy reports; it never decides dosing.

Paths and permission names on this page are proposals. Every request below is on the data listener (ns-api, or single) unless it says the owner's listener (ns-tenant-admin, or API_SECRET on single). Registration is per tenant: it affects only that tenant's site and data and is never an operator action (authority AU6, maintainer, 2026-10-26).

docs.title: 1. Files
docs.text: file what it is specs/sync/controller-state-model.schema.json the registration grammar (§3) specs/sync/hub-capabilities.schema.json the capability document (§4) specs/sync/registration-submit.schema.json requests, responses, stored registrations, definitions and instances, fallback, write replies, and the conformance case shapes specs/sync/controller-instance.schema.json the instance document (§8) specs/sync/shared-slots.yaml the shared slot list the well-known catalogue ships (§9) specs/quirks/quirk.schema.json, specs/quirks/*.yaml the quirks registry (§16) specs/sync/registrations/{loop,trio,androidaps}.yaml the well-known registrations, generated by make schema-sync-model specs/sync/registrations/fixtures/example-testcontroller.yaml a synthetic registration that uses every grammar rule specs/sync/conformance/ 186 synthetic cases (§19) tools/nsschema/negotiate.py, instances.py, quirks_registration.py reference decision functions; they check that the cases are self-consistent and are not a hub tools/nsschema/test_registration_{negotiation,instances,quirks}.py the gates

docs.title: 2. Two tiers
docs.text:
tier who writes it purpose what changes for the controller well-known the hub, generated from measurement today's writers are described as they are nothing controller-owned the controller, per release typed definitions for features unique to that controller, and the hub API derived from them it submits a registration when it wants typed support

The hub ships the well-known registrations and serves them at /.well-known/nightscout/controllers. Precedence is controller-published, then operator-declared, then structurally inferred. A registration is an affordance: what a controller may sync, how often and with which filters (cadence, queryProfile) is declared by the controller, and the hub honours a declaration it can bound.

docs.title: 3. The grammar
docs.text:
A registration (apiVersion: nightscout.dev/sync/v1) declares:

  • documents: the composite documents it writes, each with a structural discriminator (a devicestatus carrying a loop object rather than an openaps one) and the observation primitives it decomposes to. The free-text device string is never the discriminator.
  • stateSpans: one entry per intent kind; its meaning is specified in L3.
  • composition: how overlapping intents combine, as reported by the controller (reportedBy: controller, hubComputes: false).
  • commands: transport, whether the hub is in the path, authorisation, expiry, acknowledgement.
  • replayInputs: every dosing input the controller could supply, with a status and a path; an input it has but does not publish has a null path.
  • settings: the effective-dated configuration snapshot it publishes.
  • extensions: controller-specific typed data under reverse-DNS namespaces.
  • cadence, queryProfile and sensitivity.

Rules:

# rule G1 Must-ignore. Within a grammar major, a reader keeps members it does not know as written and does not interpret or serve them. No object in the grammar is closed. G2 Typed declarations. A typed field carries type, a restricted JSON Schema fragment (type, enum, minimum, maximum, format, items, properties, required; closed; an object lists its properties), or typeRef to a Nightscout-published definition such as a ControllerSettings field; plus unit, range, horizon, sensitivity and evidence. settings.fields[] and replayInputs[] take a name or a typed declaration; a carrier's paths[] take a path or a typed path {path, …} with the same typing members (state and intent S6). An extension or extension field without a type is rejected. A field with no sensitivity label falls under sensitivity.unlabelledPolicy, withhold when absent. G3 Open vocabularies. endedEncoding, command transport, replayInputs[].status, the discriminator test and endReasons take a shared value or {value: other, controllerTerm}; initiators.values take the controller's own strings, which are not a shared list, or the same other form (state and intent S8). A hub renders an unknown term as "other: term" instead of rejecting the registration. G4 Per-element versions. Each stateSpans kind and each extension may declare version, or versions (served, one stored, optional lossless mappings). Without a declared mapping nothing is converted. G5 Horizons. Documents, kinds, fields, settings and extensions may declare a horizon: cycle, span, effective-dated, definition or aggregate, each with its own cadence and retention. availability includes experimental, stored as declared with no well-known mapping and no long-term promise.

The well-known registrations carry typeRef only where the ControllerSettings definition was read from the controller's own algorithm family, and horizons only on the devicestatus document (cycle) and settings (effective-dated). They declare no kind versions.

docs.title: 4. The capability document
docs.text:
GET /.well-known/nightscout/sync, beside the catalogue at /.well-known/nightscout/controllers (RFC 8615). It is unauthenticated, cacheable and about the hub software, not a person. Under TENANCY_MODE=multi each tenant's host serves the same deployment-level content. It never lists a tenant's registrations.

member states grammar.versions[] each grammar major the hub reads and the minor it implements; a registration carries no minor grammar.interprets[] the grammar members the hub interprets, as dotted paths with * for an array item or map key; an entry covers its subtree. It covers at least apiVersion, kind, metadata.vendor, metadata.product, metadata.tier, spec.cadence, spec.documents.*.collection and spec.documents.*.decomposesTo horizons.classes[], horizons.availability[] the horizon classes and availability values the hub stores typeFragment.keywords[], typeFragment.formats[] the type keywords and formats the hub can store, validate and index; includes type limits maxRegistrationBytes (RFC 8785 canonical JSON), maxExtensions, maxFieldsPerExtension, maxTypeDepth wellKnown.catalogue, wellKnown.kinds[] each shipped registration's vendor, product, version range and href wellKnown.slots, wellKnown.mappings[] the shared slot list (§9) and the catalogue mappings for older versions (§16) submit.href, submit.tiers, submit.permissions where a controller-owned registration is submitted, and the permissions it needs; absent when the hub takes no submissions instances present when the hub serves definitions and instances (§7–§8): leaseSeconds (at least 60), the instance id form (uuid-v4), the roles and channels it grants, and label bounds commands present when the hub offers the command record (commands CM31): href, fetch (a URI template naming {instanceId}) and proposals when it takes proposals; maxExpirySeconds (CM3) and maxPayloadBytes (CM5); liveTransports, the transports it sends fetch-now signals on (CM28); and minFetchIntervalSeconds (CM29). Absent: a controller has no hub command path and keeps its own transports

The document is must-ignore like the grammar. Its vocabularies (horizon classes, availability, keywords, formats) are closed lists that match the grammar's.

A controller reads the capability document and its registration at launch and after a controller release, never on a timer, on a lease renewal or because a request was refused.

docs.title: 5.1 Identity and methods
docs.text:
A registration's identity within a tenant is (metadata.vendor, metadata.product). versionRange is an attribute: a new release updates the same registration. metadata.softwareId is proposed as a further attribute (maintainer, 2026-10-26): the reverse-DNS id of the software in the same form as the RFC 7591 software_id Nocturne's client registration and known-app directory use (org.loopkit.loop), compared exactly, so a hub can join who wrote a record with what it means on one key (controller descriptions §2.2). It is optional and not part of the identity. Whether two products may share one, and whether a hub checks it against the credential's registered client, are open (§18). The product resource is <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>, each segment percent-encoded. The owner's actions use the same paths on every deployment, served on the owner's listener (maintainer, 2026-10-26; authority §4).

method who meaning precondition PUT controller create or update If-None-Match: * to create; If-Match: <etag> to update GET controller the stored registration with its current element results, binding and credential kind none DELETE controller retire If-Match POST …/retire owner retire (maintainer, 2026-10-26: the owner's retire is a named action like the others, so on single, where one API_SECRET holder may be both, the request says which is acting) If-Match POST …/block owner block If-Match; If-None-Match: * when nothing is stored POST …/unblock, …/release, …/transfer, …/free-namespaces owner authority §4 If-Match

docs.title: 5.2 Order of checks
docs.text:
1. Authorisation (403). The permission, then the binding: any credential other than the one the registration is bound to is refused not-registration-owner for an update or retire. An owner action is authorised by its listener and refused not-authorised elsewhere.
  2. Preconditions. None sent: 428. A failed one: 412 with the current etag and state. Retiring an identity with nothing stored: 404. Then the owner's block: a write to a blocked identity is 403 blocked-by-owner. The block is checked after the preconditions, so a controller holding the etag from before the block gets 412 with current.state: blocked. A pre-emptive block stores no registration, so a create's If-None-Match: * passes and the block answers 403.
  3. The registration as a whole, each rejecting it entirely and storing nothing (422 unless stated): apiVersion not among grammar.versions (unsupported-grammar-major); wrong kind, or grammar-invalid outside spec.extensions (invalid-registration); identity differing from the resource (identity-mismatch); a tier other than controller-owned (wrong-tier); over maxRegistrationBytes (413) or maxExtensions (limit-exceeded).
  4. Each element (§5.3).
flowchart LR
  accTitle: Order of checks for a registration write
  accDescr: A write is checked for authorisation first, then its preconditions, then the owner's block, then the registration as a whole, and only then element by element. The first check that fails answers, and nothing is stored for a failure before the elements; elements are accepted or refused one at a time.
  w([PUT or DELETE of a registration]) --> auth{permission and binding}
  auth -- no --> r403[403 not-authorised or not-registration-owner]
  auth -- yes --> pre{precondition sent and current}
  pre -- none --> r428[428]
  pre -- stale --> r412[412 with the current etag and state]
  pre -- yes --> block{blocked by the owner}
  block -- yes --> rb[403 blocked-by-owner]
  block -- no --> whole{registration as a whole valid}
  whole -- no --> r422[422 or 413, nothing stored]
  whole -- yes --> el[each element accepted or refused, §5.3]
  classDef refuse fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#b42318,color:#1a1a1a
  classDef ok fill:#e6f4ea,stroke:#3b7a4a,color:#1a1a1a
  class r403,r428,r412,rb,r422 refuse
  class el ok

docs.title: 5.3 Elements and their results
docs.text:
element id from carrier when not accepted stateSpans/<kind, else category> spec.stateSpans[] its wire (write: carrier); none when wire is null extensions/<namespace> spec.extensions its carrier; none when it declares none settings.fields/<name> a typed settings.fields[] entry written as today, name-only (write: untyped) replayInputs/<input> a typed replayInputs[] entry written as today, name-only (write: untyped)

Everything else (documents, cadence, composition, commands, query profile, sensitivity, untyped settings and inputs) belongs to the registration as a whole.

Each element is accepted, accepted-with-ignored-members (with the ignored members as dotted paths), or rejected with reasons. Ignored members are those the grammar does not define plus those interprets does not cover; they are kept as written. Ignored members outside any element are listed at registration level. An element is not-interpreted when a member that defines it is ignored: a kind's category; an extension's fields, version/versions and each field's name, type and typeRef; a typed setting's or input's name and type. Otherwise an element is rejected for:

reason when namespace-not-owned the credential has stated namespace roots and none covers the namespace (authority §5) namespace-claimed another registration on the tenant holds the namespace, whatever its state untyped-extension an extension without a type declaration unsupported-type-keyword a keyword or format outside typeFragment, including in a typeRef target limit-exceeded over maxFieldsPerExtension or maxTypeDepth invalid-element an extension that fails the grammar; for a stateSpans kind, a restated member of a wellKnownRef entry or a sameAs that breaks §9's checks (any other grammar failure outside spec.extensions rejects the whole registration as invalid-registration, §5.2) version-plan-invalid, unsupported-availability, unsupported-horizon checked only where the hub interprets them version-conflict, unknown-well-known-kind §7 unknown-shared-slot §9

Reason codes are an open vocabulary (other with the hub's term); detail is for people.

The outcome is accepted when every element is accepted and partial when at least one is rejected; both store the registration as written (201 on create, 200 on update). An accepted element may carry carrierView (§13). A controller that does not know an element result, reason or carrierView value treats the element as not accepted.

docs.title: 5.4 Etag and idempotency
docs.text: The etag is sha256: over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of {registration, state, boundTo} (registration and boundTo null for a pre-emptive block), so it changes on every change of content, state or binding. The credential kind, the binding event and freed namespaces are stored beside it and are not in it. A request whose content and state are already stored is a no-op (200, noop: true, the stored etag), so a create retried after a lost response succeeds. A stale If-Match with different content is 412 stale-etag; If-None-Match: * over different content is 412 registration-exists. The hub evaluates a stored registration against its current capabilities on every read, so an element's result can change after a hub upgrade while the stored registration and its etag do not.

docs.title: 5.5 Retire
docs.text: The bound controller retires with DELETE and api:registrations:delete; the owner may also retire, with POST …/retire (§5.1). Retiring sets the state to retired, changes the etag, and keeps the declaration and the binding frozen: data already stored under it stays stored and readable as declared, and no typed write is accepted for its elements. Its namespaces stay claimed until the owner frees them. A later PUT with the retired etag reactivates it; a freed namespace is claimed again only if no other registration holds it by then, and otherwise that extension is rejected namespace-claimed. The controller writes its carriers from the moment it retires.

docs.title: 6. The controller's side: fallback and refused writes
docs.text:
An element is written through the typed API only when the response to this registration has outcome accepted or partial and the element's result is accepted or accepted-with-ignored-members. Everything else falls back to the element's carrier (§5.3): a rejected element; an unknown result, reason or carrierView; a rejected registration; a failed precondition; a retired or blocked registration; no response (a submit answered 429 or any 5xx is no response); no capability document, no submit, or a grammar major the hub does not list.

A controller that depends on an ignored member may treat that element as not accepted.

An accepted element whose carrierView is served is written typed only. One whose view is not served is written typed only, or typed and as its carrier when the element declares dualWriteLink (typedIdPath, carrierIdPath): the record is linked by (instance id, the controller's record id), so counting and de-duplication follow the link. Writing both is for an element with no declared carrier mapping, and while an app moves over.

A typed write refused for load (429 or any 5xx, with or without Retry-After) is retried with backoff, no sooner than Retry-After when sent, until it succeeds. It is never written as its carrier, the record is not dropped and the write plan does not change, so a write the hub stored before failing cannot appear twice. Any other refusal is definite (blocked-by-owner, a retired or missing registration, instance-required, a typed route answering 404 after a hub rollback, or a 4xx the controller does not know): the controller sends that record as its carrier at once and treats the element as not accepted until its next re-check (§4).

The capability document carries everything the response depends on except the tenant's stored registrations with their bindings and blocks, the credential's grants, and whether the hub serves a carrier view of an element. A controller can predict most of the result before it submits; the response is authoritative.

docs.title: 7. Definitions
docs.text:
The product resource registers what a controller's data means. Definitions let several releases and builds of one product coexist; instances (§8) say which copy is connected.

resource method who meaning precondition <…>/<product> as §5 as §5 the product: binding, state, owner actions, namespaces, etag, element results. Its body is a definition as §5 <…>/<product>/definitions/<definitionId> PUT the credential the product is bound to add a definition, immutably If-None-Match: * only /api/v4/instances/<instanceId> PUT any credential with api:registrations:create create, renew or change an instance; the body names the product as §5 /api/v4/instances/<instanceId> DELETE the credential the instance is bound to, with api:registrations:delete release the instance and all its roles If-Match /api/v4/instances GET the owner the owner's listing (authority §4) none

A hub that advertises instances serves the added resources; one that does not serves neither, and §5 applies unchanged.

Amendment, maintainer 2026-10-26: one flat root for instances. The instance resource is /api/v4/instances/<instanceId>, beside its command fetch /api/v4/instances/<instanceId>/commands (commands CM32), so one running copy has one path root. Before this amendment it was <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>/instances/<instanceId>. Definitions stay under the product, because a definition belongs to one product. The instance body names its product (product: {vendor, product}, controller-instance.schema.json); the order of checks below reads the product from it, and a renewal naming a product other than the stored instance's is 422 invalid-instance. The instance is looked up within the request's tenant, as every tenant resource is (CM6). The id is a random UUID v4 (identity §2), so a copy keeps one path for its life. cgm-remote-monitor's draft #8857 serves the earlier nested path.

Identity. The definition id is defined in identity §2. A product PUT's accepted or partial response names the definitionId the hub computed. Every definition the hub accepts is stored content-addressed: the product's current registration, every registration a product update replaced, and every definition added by PUT. Any number coexist under one product.

Adding one. Order of checks: (1) authorisation: the owner never adds one (403 not-authorised); the permission; a registered product (404); the product's binding (403 not-registration-owner). A definition PUT never binds a released product, because a binding changes the product's etag and a definition never does; the controller re-binds with a product PUT. (2) If-None-Match: * (428 otherwise); a blocked product is 403 blocked-by-owner, a retired one 409 product-retired. (3) The body's hash equals the path id (422 definition-id-mismatch), then §5.2 step 3. (4) Element results as §5.3, plus the rules below. An identical retry is a 200 no-op. Adding a definition never changes the product resource or its etag, so instances of one product never contend on it.

Namespaces belong to the product across all its stored definitions: another product's definition declaring any of them is rejected namespace-claimed until the owner frees it.

One element at one version has one meaning. Within one product, an element of a new definition (a stateSpans kind or an extension namespace) whose stored version equals that of the same element in a stored definition, and whose meaning differs, is rejected version-conflict. This applies to definition PUTs and to product PUTs, where an update is compared with the registration it replaces, which stays stored. A different meaning needs a new version; definitions that agree, or declare different versions, coexist. The version compared is version or versions.stored; an element that declares none is one unversioned version. Typed settings fields and replay inputs carry no version in grammar v1 and are not compared.

members that are meaning not meaning stateSpans kind category, kind, slot, exclusiveWithinSlot, coexistsWith, overlay, supersedes, states, endReasons, wire, dualWriteLink, requested, applied, initiators, definitions, acceptsFromHub, horizon, sameAs description, evidence, availability, version/versions, members the grammar does not define extension carrier, dualWriteLink, horizon, fields (compared by name) description, evidence, availability, version/versions extension field name, type, typeRef, unit, range, horizon, sensitivity description, evidence

Inside a meaning member, description, evidence and a carrier's writtenWhen are prose and not compared, and order is not meaning: an array of strings compares as a sorted set, an array of objects as the sorted list of their canonical forms. A carrier path written {path: x} with no typing member compares as the bare string x; one that declares a unit or type does not. availability is a promise level, so an experimental kind can be released at the same version. sensitivity is meaning, so a later definition cannot relabel data stored under an earlier one.

Well-known references. A stateSpans entry whose kind is exactly a kind of the hub's catalogue names it instead of copying it: wellKnownRef: {catalogue, kind, version}, where catalogue is the id of an entry in the capability document's wellKnown.kinds[], kind is the catalogue kind's kind (else its category) and version its stored version. wellKnownRef is additive under must-ignore. The entry carries only category and kind (the catalogue kind's), the reference, availability, description and evidence; a restated member is rejected invalid-element. Its meaning, version, slot, carrier and sameAs are the catalogue kind's, so an identical copy agrees with a reference and a differing copy at that version is version-conflict. A reference to a kind the catalogue does not have at that version is rejected unknown-well-known-kind, and the controller writes that kind's carrier. Only a catalogue kind that declares a version can be referenced; the three well-known registrations declare none, so none of their kinds can be referenced until the generator versions them.

docs.title: 8. Instances
docs.text:
Identity. The instance id is defined in identity §2: a random lowercase UUID v4 supplied by the controller.

Body (controller-instance.schema.json): apiVersion, kind: ControllerInstance, definitionId (a stored definition of this product, else 422 unknown-definition), roles[] and labels{}. An instance carries no hardware identifiers; anything identifying a controller reports is a typed, sensitivity-labelled field of its definition.

Observed alias. The hub may record the free-text devicestatus.device it sees in an instance's writes as an observed alias, labelled {level: identifying, category: device}. It is withheld by default: absent from the owner's default listing (shown only when the owner asks for withheld members), never in the capability document, never in a default export, and never the instance's identity.

Order of checks for PUT. (1) Authorisation: the owner never writes an instance (403 not-authorised); the permission; a registered product (404); an existing instance's binding (403 not-registration-owner). An instance is bound to the subject that created it (or the shared secret on single), not to the product's binding, so a development build with its own subject may run a copy of a registered product. (2) Preconditions: none is 428; If-None-Match: * over a different stored body is 412; an If-Match that is not the current etag is 412 stale-etag with the current etag and lease; then a blocked product is 403 blocked-by-owner and a retired one 409 product-retired. (3) The instance as a whole, each 422 with nothing stored: the id form (invalid-instance-id), labels (invalid-label), the schema (invalid-instance, including a role without provenance and a (channel, role) claimed twice), unknown-definition. (4) Each role (§9).

Lease. Each create or renewal sets leaseExpiresAt to now plus instances.leaseSeconds; the response carries it and per-role results (outcome accepted, or partial when a role is refused; 201 on create, 200 on renewal). An instance that stops renewing lapses and holds no roles, with no housekeeping. A renewal is not a capability re-check.

Etag. sha256: over the canonical JSON of {instance, boundTo, granted}. The lease is outside it, so a renewal that changes nothing keeps it (noop: true) and a retried renewal still matches. A role granted on renewal, moved by the owner, or dropped by a rebind (§9) changes it, so the instance learns of the change through a 412 on its next renewal, and two owner actions racing on one instance meet 412. A create retried with the same body by the same subject is a renewal.

DELETE releases the instance and all its roles. Records it wrote keep its id.

docs.title: 9. Channels, roles and provenance
docs.text:
A role is {channel, role, provenance}:

  • source: the instance writes the channel's typed records as their source of record.
  • command-sink: the instance accepts hub-originated commands for the channel. Only on a channel whose kind declares acceptsFromHub.channels with command, else not-a-command-channel.
  • {value: other, controllerTerm}: any other role, such as an agent's. A hub grants only the roles its capability document lists (unsupported-role otherwise); a bare unknown string is invalid.

provenance is required and closed: device or simulated. One instance may mix them (a development build with a real CGM and a simulated pump). An unknown provenance refuses that role (unknown-provenance), never the instance. Only device-provenance data is therapy data in default views and exports.

Channels. For a stateSpans kind that declares a slot:

  • if the slot is on the hub's shared slot list (wellKnown.slots, shipped from specs/sync/shared-slots.yaml: override, loopMode, temporaryTarget), the channel is that shared slot, contended across products;
  • if the kind declares sameAs: <shared slot> on a hub that interprets sameAs and lists that slot, the channel is the shared slot;
  • otherwise the slot is the product's own channel, <vendor>/<product>/<slot>: on the wire the channel keeps the slot's name and its roles are scoped to the product; instances of one product contend on it, and equal names from different products do not.

Every other element's channel is <vendor>/<product>/<element id>. A slot name containing / derives no shared channel. A role on a channel the instance's definition does not derive is refused unknown-channel. Two slots are joined only by a listed name or a declared sameAs, never because their names look alike: AndroidAPS's runningMode and Loop's and Trio's loopMode stay separate until a definition or a catalogue mapping says otherwise, as do names that differ only in case. The owner's listing records each unlisted slot name used by two or more products as slotNameObservations, for the catalogue to act on.

sameAs checks, at a product or definition PUT: a shared slot the hub does not list, or a hub with no list, is unknown-shared-slot; a sameAs without a slot (or with / in it), on a slot whose own name is a different shared slot, or disagreeing with another entry of the definition that names the same slot, is invalid-element. A refused element goes as its carrier and its slot derives no channel, so it never joins another product's slot by name instead.

Exclusivity. Among live device-provenance instances of active products on the tenant, each (channel, role) has one holder. A second claimant is refused that role role-held; its other roles are granted, and it writes the elements on that channel as their carriers. The hub shows the overlap on the owner's listing (channel, role, claimant, holder) until the claimant drops the claim or lapses; holder: null when the holder has lapsed or dropped the role. simulated roles never contend with device roles or with each other.

Command-sink binding. Which instance may hold a device command-sink role, and what a change of a product's binding does to it, is authority §6. Source roles are open to any permitted subject.

Handoff. A role passes when its holder drops it (a renewal without it, or DELETE), when the holder's lease lapses, or when the owner transfers it. A lapsed or dropped role is not auto-assigned: a claimant is granted it on its own next renewal, which re-evaluates every claim.

Command routing. Where a command for a channel goes, and its refusals, are commands §2.

The hub never decides dosing. Exclusivity decides only which instance is the typed source of record for a channel and where a command for that channel is routed. A claimant refused a role keeps running and keeps writing its carriers; the hub records what each instance reports. devicestatus and other documents are not channels: writes to them are attributed by instance, and loop-status exclusivity is not specified until devicestatus decomposition is typed.

docs.title: 10. Labels
docs.text: String keys to string values, which distinguish, select and filter instances. A key is <reverse-DNS namespace>/<name> (com.example.testcontroller/rig); labels are not subject to namespace claims. The prefix dev.nightscout/ is reserved for dev.nightscout/purpose (therapy, development, lab, research), dev.nightscout/build (release, dev) and dev.nightscout/migration-group (an opaque string shared by the old and new phone of one migration). A reader reads an unlisted value of the first two as other. Another key under the prefix, a key not in the form, a non-string value, or labels over instances.labels bounds are refused invalid-label. Labels carry no names, device names or serials. Provenance, never a label, decides what is therapy data.

docs.title: 11. Typed writes and attribution
docs.text:
A hub that advertises instances requires an instance id on every typed write (proposed as a request header). An instance-less typed write is refused 422 instance-required, a definite refusal (§6). The writing instance must be live (409 not-live) and hold source on the element's channel (409 role-held when another instance does, role-not-granted otherwise), so a refused claimant's record goes as its carrier. An accepted typed record carries its instance, its definition and the role's provenance.

Writes with no instance (older controllers, and anything the well-known tier describes) are attributed to an implicit unregistered instance of the product, which holds no roles and is never refused for exclusivity. Exclusivity never blocks a carrier write, from any instance. Readers attribute typed records to the registration and its bound credential; a namespace string proves nothing about authorship.

The ids each write returns, and how a re-send is matched, are in identity §1.

docs.title: 12. Read selection
docs.text:
Writes need no selection: each instance names its definition. A view chooses, per versioned element of a product, the version it shows:

  1. the operator's capability document limits what is accepted at all: only versions of stored definitions whose element the hub accepts today are candidates;
  2. the owner's pin, for the site's default views;
  3. the newest version run by a live instance holding a device source role on the element's channel;
  4. the newest stored version.

A view with a label selector (every selector key must have that value) uses only the live instances that match, whatever their provenance, and no pin. "Newest" compares dot-separated parts, numeric parts as numbers and before text. Pins are the owner's pin-version and unpin-version, a resource of their own per product with its own etag (If-None-Match: * for the first pin, If-Match after), so a pin never changes the product's etag or stored data. A pin names a version some stored definition stores (422 unknown-version).

docs.title: 13. Projected views for older readers
docs.text:
An accepted element's carrierView: served requires a declared mapping: the catalogue's carrier for a referenced well-known kind, the kind's wire, or an extension's carrier. A hub that would serve a view of an element without one reports not-served, and the controller writes as §6 says. For a served element, each typed record is served to API v1 and v3 readers as a projected document in the carrier's shape: the collection, eventType, start time and duration in the wire's unit (or its indefinite sentinel) from the mapping, and nothing the mapping does not declare. The projected document is labelled projectedFrom: {definitionId, element, entities}, is never stored as a source, and is read-only (409 projected-read-only); its ids are in identity I8. Where one carrier document is projected from several entities, the id is the primary entity's and entities lists them all. A projection without a declared mapping is refused 409 no-carrier-mapping.

A projected view is not a conversion between typed versions (G4).

Prior art, read-derived at Nocturne 42275c812: V4ToLegacyProjectionService and LegacyTreatmentTables serve v1–v3 reads from V4 records, project a meal bolus from a bolus and a carb intake under the bolus's id, and tell legacy mirrors from V4-native records with a NativeOnly filter; the projected treatment carries no projection marker.

docs.title: 14. Retention
docs.text: A definition may be removed only when no stored record references it, no live instance runs it, and it is not the product's current registration (otherwise definition-referenced, definition-in-use or definition-current). Each record's declared horizon retention decides when the record goes.

docs.title: 15. Binding, credentials and the owner
docs.text: The binding and credential kind, the owner's actions, the authorisation of registrations and namespaces are maintained in the authority specification §3–§5.

docs.title: 16. Version-scoped quirks
docs.text:
The quirks registry records how stored documents deviate, per collection and project, with measured prevalence.

# rule Q1 affects. It applies to stored documents and to declarations (slot names, units, vocabulary). An entry may carry affects: [{vendor, product, versions}], versions a range over the vendor's own version strings (*, or whitespace-separated comparators =, >=, >, <=, < that must all hold; dot-separated parts compare numerically, numbers before text), stated only where the corpus or source shows it, else unmeasured with the reason. seen lists versions the evidence shows. Each claim says measured or read-derived. versionSource says where make schema-quirks reads a version: in the same document, or by co-occurrence (the nearest version-bearing document of the same site within a window), labelled as co-occurrence and never copied into a range. Entries without affects keep their project-level attribution. Q2 Catalogue for older versions, sameAs for newer. A newer definition declares its own mapping (sameAs, §9). Versions released before registration get it from a registry entry with applies_to: declarations (declaration: {member: slot, value, sameAs}, with affects), published as wellKnown.mappings[] ({quirk, vendor, product, versions, slot, sameAs}). When an older controller's write is described by its well-known registration and the hub knows the writer's version and it is in versions, the hub attributes the records to the shared slot. The means by which the hub identifies the writer and its version are not specified; with no known version it applies no mapping. A mapping changes which channel records are shown on and which overlaps the owner sees, never whether they are stored. Q3 Recorded, never silent. Each mapping the hub applies is recorded on the reply and on the stored record or document as quirksApplied: [{quirk, member, action, sameAs?}], action one of moved-to-identifier, dropped, same-as. A write whose channel a sameAs decided carries slotMapping: {slot, channel, by}, by being declared, catalogue (with the entry's id) or name. Q4a Entry members. Beside affects, an entry may carry retired, and mapping: {action, flag, erasesEvidence} for what a hub does with the quirk: QUIRK-TREATMENTS-006 and QUIRK-ENTRIES-004 carry {action: move-to-identifier, flag: UUID_HANDLING, erasesEvidence: true}, because a mapped write no longer shows the quirk in storage. QUIRK-TREATMENTS-007 (Trio's treatment model sending its UUID as id) is a measured, version-scoped entry with no mapping: cgm-remote-monitor matches such treatments by created_at + eventType, and whether Trio should send identifier goes to PROPOSAL-REG-CONTROLLERS. Q4 Lifecycle. proposed → active → historical → retired. make schema-quirks writes which statuses the measurement supports and why not the others; make schema-quirks-check fails a historical or retired claim it does not support and never fails a proposed one. historical needs no recent document, zero live instances of an affected version in a hub's de-identified instance listing (unmeasured without one), and a detector whose evidence the hub's mapping does not erase (an entry whose mapping has erasesEvidence: true becomes historical only through Q3 records). retired also needs no stored document that depends on the mapping. Recent is within RECENT_DAYS = 365 days of the newest snapshot's collection date. Declaration entries are measured by a hub's recorded mappings.

No declaration entry is listed: which slots share a meaning is evidence for the controller authors (PROPOSAL-REG-CONTROLLERS). Candidates, read from the well-known registrations and not confirmed by any controller author:

candidate slots differs in loopMode Loop loopMode (dosingEnabled, carried by the profile), Trio loopMode (DosingMode, devicestatus), AndroidAPS runningMode (RunningMode, treatments OpenAPS Offline) name, carrier, states; AndroidAPS's coexists with profileSwitch, temporaryTarget and scene override Loop and Trio override carrier eventType (Temporary Override, Exercise); Loop's coexists with preMeal, Trio's with temporaryTarget temporaryTarget Trio and AndroidAPS temporaryTarget coexistence lists temporaryTarget or override Loop preMeal a Loop override preset with its own slot and no carrier of its own none AndroidAPS profileSwitch, scene no counterpart in Loop or Trio

How the _id entries are applied on a write is in identity I9.

docs.text:
Per app, read from source: compatibility.

docs.title: 18. Open choices
docs.text:
Rules the specification chose that await the maintainer's confirmation:

  • Product (§5): the cases assume a controller does not treat an element as not accepted merely because it depends on an ignored member. The binding and owner choices are in authority §9.
  • Definitions and instances (§7–§12): a definition PUT never binds a released product; definitions and instances are refused for a retired product; the instance etag covers granted roles; every listed role, including an other role, is exclusive among device instances; a typed write needs a granted source role; the owner transfers only to a live instance already claiming the role with device provenance; pins are their own resource; "newest" is numeric by part; a label selector ignores provenance and pins; the current registration keeps its definition from removal; typed settings fields and replay inputs are outside version-conflict; wellKnownRef needs a versioned catalogue kind; the permission names reuse api:registrations:create and delete.
  • Quirks (§16): the shipped slot list holds the three names already used identically; unknown-shared-slot refuses the element rather than falling back to the slot's own name; catalogue mappings need a known writer version; historical needs a hub's instance listing; a mapping that erases its evidence makes historical depend on Q3 records; a proposed entry never fails the check; declaration entries are measured only by hub records.
  • Identity: two choices are listed in identity §5.
  • metadata.softwareId (§5.1, proposed 2026-10-26): whether two products may share one; whether a hub checks it against the credential's registered OAuth client where the hub has one.

Open: the contract per tenancy mode (SPEC-REG-MODES), the mechanics of registration state across a site's move into a tenant, whose binding rule authority §3 states (SPEC-REG-MIGRATE). The command API is proposed in the commands specification.

docs.title: L3 State and intent: what was requested, applied and active, who started it, and why it ended
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at a8f03c290.

Contributor-facing. Living specification, current at main 92a7d31b (2026-10-18). Layer L3 of the platform index; terms are in the glossary. The grammar members named here are part of the registration specification §3; how a hub accepts them is there too. Decisions: D18 (the hub observes, the controller composes) and the maintainer's 2026-10-18 decision on agent initiators (execution plan §2.6.3 row 17). Queue: SPEC-STATE-INTENT.

Specification 4 of 8 in the reading order; after registration, whose grammar it uses, and before commands. Expect rules S1–S12 and A1–A13, the declared kinds per controller, composition, what is active at a time, and the conformance cases.

A controller manages intent: a preset is activated, several intents run at once and combine, the controller applies something that may differ from what was asked, and the intent ends for a reason. Nightscout's collections manage entities. This page says how a controller declares its intent model, so that a reader can tell what was requested, what was applied, who started it and why it ended, and what the hub may and may not conclude from the records. Status: rules S1–S12 are specified; the active-state rules A1–A13 are proposed and specified with cases; §3, §4 and §7 are evidenced; §5 is proposed; none is implemented.

The evidence is the intent and workflow landscape, read from Loop, Trio, iAPS and AndroidAPS source and measured where it says so.

docs.title: 1. What entity records lose
docs.text:
# property what it means how today's documents lose it P1 definition identity an activation refers to a preset by a stable id presets are copied into the instance, or referenced by name only P2 concurrent slots and composition several intents active at once, combined by a controller rule one collection, one "latest wins" reading per eventType P3 requested versus applied what was asked, what the device or algorithm accepted, what it computed one document is both request and effect, or the effect is elsewhere and unlinked P4 end reason expired, cancelled, superseded, deleted before start, ended by a trigger "ended" is a shortened duration, a delete, or a zero-duration record P5 initiator phone, watch, shortcut, automation, caregiver, remote kept locally or in debug logs; on the wire only free-text enteredBy P6 command lifecycle request, validate, apply, acknowledge, with a correlation id no request record; success visible only as the resulting entity; failure as free text

Every rule below exists so that one of P1–P6 survives into the record.

docs.title: 2. Rules
docs.text: # rule S1 The hub observes; the controller composes. Overlapping intents are combined by a controller-specific rule that depends on algorithm settings. The hub records the result the controller reports and never computes it: composition is declared with reportedBy: controller and hubComputes: false, with where the result is published (result, or null) and whether it names the intents it came from (linkedToIntents). rule is the controller's rule as read from its source, informational only. S2 One declaration per intent kind. A stateSpans entry declares one kind: category (open, and the only required member; what the hub renders and queries it under) and kind (the controller's own name). Its horizon is span unless it declares another. An entry may also carry dualWriteLink (registration §6) and wellKnownRef (registration §7). S3 Slots. slot names the exclusivity group. exclusiveWithinSlot: at most one instance is active in the slot at a time. coexistsWith: the slots that can be active at the same time; how they combine is S1. overlay: a timed instance applies over an open-ended one, which applies again when the timed one ends. supersedes: a later instance of this kind from this controller ends an overlapping earlier one, as the controller does it. The hub reads these to render and query the controller's own records; it never reconciles between controllers. sameAs names the shared slot a slot means; how a slot becomes a channel for roles, and the sameAs checks, are registration §9. S4 States. The vocabulary is scheduled (exists, not yet started), active and ended, written as a list of strings; registrations generated before 2026-10-12 used active and inactive. S5 End reasons. Shared values expired, cancelled, superseded, deletedBeforeStart, endedByTrigger, or other, which requires controllerTerm and is rendered "other: term". Any reason may also carry the controller's own controllerTerm (Loop declares expired as "natural"). endedByTrigger lists its triggers, a list of strings whose vocabulary is carbs, glucoseAbove, glucoseBelow, loopOff, chain. S6 The wire carrier. wire says how today's documents carry instances of the kind: the collection; eventType, or documentIdentifier for a single named document (such as one in the v3 settings collection); a discriminator (path and test: exists, is-object, equals with a value, or {value: other, controllerTerm}); paths, each a dotted path string or a typed path {path, unit, type or typeRef} that carries the typing members of a field declaration (registration G2), so a carrier field can declare its unit (AndroidAPS declares timeshift in milliseconds); a typed path with no typing member names the same field, with the same meaning, as the bare string; vocabularies (closed value sets by path), unpublishedFields and writtenWhen; durationField, the path that carries the duration, and durationUnit (seconds, minutes, milliseconds); identity, the fields that identify one instance across amendments; indefinite, how an open-ended instance is written; endedEncoding, how an early end is written (amend-duration, delete-and-repost, repost-same-created_at, zero-duration-record, sampled-state, or {value: other, controllerTerm}); cancelBeforeStartEncoding (delete, soft-delete, zero-duration-record); and endReasonPath, or null when the reason is not sent and can only be inferred from the encoding. wire: null means the controller keeps the intent and publishes no instance record. S7 Requested and applied are separate. requested says where the request is recorded when it is a different record from the applied effect; applied says where the controller reports what it applied; either is null when not published. Both are carriers with the members S6 lists, except the ones only wire has (identity, indefinite and the end encodings), so each declares its own durationField and durationUnit: Loop's applied override reports override.duration in seconds remaining while its wire override's duration is in minutes. A carrier's linkToRequest names the field that links an applied record to its request, or null. A request record alone does not show that anything was applied: AndroidAPS writes an effective profile switch only after the pump accepts the profile switch, and a profile switch with none following is one that failed or is pending. S8 Initiators. initiators gives the controller's vocabulary name, its values, the wirePath that carries it (or null), and a wireProxy where one wire value stands in for one initiator. Each value is a string in the controller's own vocabulary, which is not a shared list, so any string is valid; a value outside that vocabulary is written {value: other, controllerTerm} and rendered "other: term". Decided 2026-10-18: no agent value is added to any initiator vocabulary, and an agent initiator takes that other form; a shared value is named once the corpus or a lab shows one in use. No controller records an agent as initiator today. S9 Definitions. definitions says where presets are published (or null), the idField that carries a stable id on the wire (or null), whether an instance refers to its definition by id, name or copy (referencedBy), and the fields, unpublishedFields and controllerUniqueFields. S10 Acceptance policy. acceptsFromHub says which hub-originated intent of the kind the controller acts on: channels (command, a remote command delivered to it; treatment-download, treatments other clients wrote that it reads and applies), the gating preference and its default, and whether acceptance or rejection is acknowledged where the hub can see it. Only a kind accepting command can carry a command-sink role. S11 The controller's command contract. commands[] declares each path by which commands reach the controller: transport (apns, sms, nightscout-settings, nightscout-treatment, or {value: other, controllerTerm}), availability (the AndroidAPS nightscout-settings path is dev-only: in the 4.0.0 prereleases and absent from the latest release, 3.4.2.6), hubInPath (no, optional, yes), authorisation, expiry, acknowledgement (states, replyChannel, correlationId, failureRecord) and evidence. The hub's own command API and the proposal record in front of a command are the commands specification. S12 A kind's meaning is versioned. Every member above except description, evidence, availability and the version members is meaning: a different meaning at the same version is rejected version-conflict (registration §7). A controller that changes how it encodes an end, a unit or a vocabulary declares a new version of the kind.

docs.text:
controller rule (S1, informational) where the result is published Loop target = pre-meal if active, else override, else schedule; basal ×f, ISF ×1/f, carb ratio ×1/f from the override only, applied over the history window devicestatus override.currentCorrectionRange and override.multiplier, only while an override is active Trio, iAPS target = temporary target if set, else override target (unless 0 or 6), else profile; override percentage and ISF/CR scope apply regardless; a high or low temporary target also sets sensitivityRatio through halfBasalTarget devicestatus openaps.suggested ISF, CR, current_target and sensitivityRatio per loop cycle, not attributed to the intents that produced them (Trio's registration; iAPS has none) AndroidAPS a temporary target replaces the targets; a profile switch's percentage has already scaled basal, ISF and carb ratio in the effective profile switch; one profile switch, one temporary target, one running mode and one scene at a time the effective profile switch's profileJson (a Note with originalProfileName)

docs.title: 5. Effect and motivation (proposed)
docs.text:
specs/sync/therapy-effect.schema.json is a draft that separates a temporary effect from why it was asked for, so that a projection which withholds the motivation is a field selection rather than a redaction. It is not adopted as a decision; the effects and versioning analysis is its evidence. A TherapyEffect is a span (startTimestamp, endTimestamp or null while running, an id, a correlationId linking the decisions taken under it, a structural source, and supersededById when a later effect replaces it) with:

  • effect: insulinNeedsScaleFactor, basalScaleFactor, sensitivityScaleFactor, carbRatioScaleFactor, targetRange, timeShiftSeconds, smbAllowed, maxSmbMinutes, suspendDelivery. Absent means unchanged; a factor of 1.0 is not the same as absent.
  • motivation: an optional closed classification, an optional label in the person's own words, and decidedBy.
  • disclosure: effect-only, effect+classification or full, chosen by the person whose data it is.
  • provenance: the remapping rule from specs/sync/effect-remapping.yaml and whether it was lossy.

disclosure controls what a record states, not what an observer could infer from it: a recurring effect is itself a signal. The remapping is lossy for Trio's override, whose wire document carries a preset name and no effect.

docs.title: 6. What is active at a time
docs.text: How a hub answers "what was active at time t" from the records a controller wrote and the kinds it declared. Proposed, for the maintainer to confirm (§6.3, ten choices): specified with synthetic cases and a reference function (tools/nsschema/active_state.py), not implemented by any hub. The hub reports instances and which are active; it never combines them (S1).

docs.title: 6.1 Rules
docs.text:
# rule A1 Per product and kind. Instances are derived per (vendor, product) and kind, from that product's records only. Instances of two products are both reported, even on one shared slot; neither ends the other. A2 Identity makes an instance. A record belongs to a kind's requested layer by its wire carrier (collection, eventType, discriminator) and, when the kind declares a requested carrier, by that carrier too. Records whose wire.identity fields are equal are one instance; its content is the last live write the hub received for that identity. Two records with equal identity at the same instant are one instance, never two. A3 Start is the record's own time. An instance starts at its record's timeField (created_at when none is declared), never at the time in its _id or the time the hub received it (identity I3). A4 End from the declared duration. An instance ends at its start plus durationField in durationUnit. A record carrying the indefinite sentinel, or no duration, is open-ended. A5 End encodings. An amendment that shortens an instance (amend-duration, repost-same-created_at, or delete-and-repost under one identity) ends it early, with end reason cancelled; one that runs its duration ends expired. Under zero-duration-record, a zero-duration record ends the latest-starting instance of the kind and product that started strictly before it and is active at its time, with cancelled, and is not an instance itself; an instance starting at the marker's own time is not ended. The end reason describes an instance once it has ended; an amendment that shortens an instance is read as an early end, and an edit that only shortens it reads the same. A6 Deletion. A delete removes the write it names: by _id, as a delete by id carries no other field, or by identity. A soft delete (a write with isValid: false) removes its identity. An instance with no live write left is listed as ended deletedBeforeStart, and is never active and ends nothing, when the delete was received before its start; otherwise it is not reported, as a deleted document is not today. A re-post received before the delete of the record it replaces still amends the instance. A7 Supersession by start. Under supersedes, an instance ends at the start of the next instance of the same kind and product that starts after it and before its end, with superseded. Order is by start, never by arrival, so a backfilled earlier instance is ended by the later one whichever arrived first. Two instances that start at the same instant: the one whose last write was received later supersedes. A8 Overlay. Under overlay, a timed instance applies over an open-ended one without ending it; the open-ended one is not active while the timed one is, and is active again when it ends. A9 Overlap is reported, not resolved. For a kind that is exclusiveWithinSlot and declares neither supersedes nor overlay, overlapping instances are all reported active, each marked overlap. A10 Requested and applied are separate layers. Wire records matching the requested carrier give the requested layer (A2); applied records give the applied layer. Each applied record is in effect from its timeField until its own end or the next applied record of the same carrier and product, whichever is first; a record whose activeField is false ends what the earlier one put in effect. An applied carrier sampled per cycle (devicestatus) gives an applied layer only when it declares activeField; without one its values are the controller's composed result (S1) and name no intent, so no instance is reported from them. A request with no applied record is reported as requested only. A11 Units are declared, never assumed. A duration is read only in its declared durationUnit. A kind whose carrier has a duration and no unit yields no instances and is reported unreadable; the other kinds still answer. A field's unit is reported from its typed path, and a path with no unit carries none. A12 A state version. A product's state version at a time is sha256: over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of its active rows with each instance's content. It changes when an instance starts, ends or is amended, including an amendment that changes only what the instance says. It versions the hub's record of what the controller reported, not the controller's own state: an approval bound to it is checked by the hub (commands CM15), and only the controller's own validation checks its own state (D18). A13 Sampled state. A kind whose endedEncoding is sampled-state has no instance records: each record carries the current value, which holds from the record's time until the next record of the kind and product. The value reported is the first declared path's.

The rules drawn. Each panel draws one conformance case's records and its expected answer, not an application of the rule; tools/diagrams/active_state_rules.py generates them from the cases (make diagrams-svg; make diagrams-svg-check fails when one is stale).

docs.title: 6.2 What decides each measured disagreement
docs.text:
LAB-HUB-ACTIVE-STATE measured cgm-remote-monitor and Nocturne disagreeing on one synthetic record set (landscape §5). The lab ran each hub's storage and active-state code directly, Nocturne on SQLite, not either hub's HTTP write path. The rules give one answer for each; it is not always either hub's.

disagreement (measured) rule and declaration case against the hubs a temporary target followed by a cancel: cgm-remote-monitor truncates the target; Nocturne records the cancel as an open span of its own A5, for a kind declaring zero-duration-record active-state/zero-duration-ends-instance cgm-remote-monitor's answer Loop's devicestatus override duration: seconds in cgm-remote-monitor, minutes in Nocturne A3, A10, A11; Loop's applied carrier declares override.timestamp, override.active and seconds (NightscoutService StoredDosingDecision.swift:118-136) active-state/applied-duration-in-declared-unit cgm-remote-monitor's answer a timed profile switch after a permanent one: cgm-remote-monitor falls back to the permanent profile; Nocturne has none after expiry A4, A7, A8; AndroidAPS's profile switch declares duration 0 as permanent, overlay and supersedes (AndroidAPS AppRepository.kt:408-415, ProfileSwitchDao.kt:37) active-state/permanent-profile-switch-returns cgm-remote-monitor's answer AndroidAPS timeshift: milliseconds in cgm-remote-monitor, hours in Nocturne A11; the profile switch declares {path: timeshift, unit: milliseconds} active-state/field-unit-from-declaration cgm-remote-monitor's answer two temporary targets at the same millisecond: cgm-remote-monitor keeps the first; Nocturne stores both A2 for equal identity (the last received write); A7 for different identities active-state/equal-identity-same-instant neither: cgm-remote-monitor keeps the first write, the rules the last (§6.3 choice 1) an earlier open override backfilled after a later one: Nocturne leaves two open spans A7 active-state/backfill-supersedes-by-start cgm-remote-monitor's list answer

Both hubs ignore a stored Temporary Override Cancel (measured), so they agree; that careportal does not store one is read-derived. The writers that end with a zero-duration record (careportal, nightguard, iAPS) have no registration, so A5 applies to them once one declares zero-duration-record. AndroidAPS's running mode reads its duration from originalDuration in milliseconds, 0 when permanent, because its wire duration is 0 for loop modes and a 10-year placeholder for an open-ended loop-disabled mode (RunningModeExtension.kt:25-97), and it is resolved like the profile switch (AppRepository.kt:451-458).

docs.title: 6.3 Choices for the maintainer to confirm
docs.text:
1. The last received write is an instance's content (A2), so a late, stale re-send of an older version would win. The alternative, the latest by the record's own time, needs a time that changes on amendment, which no carrier declares.
  2. A record deleted after its start is not reported (A6), rather than listed as cancelled.
  3. Two instances starting at the same instant: the later received supersedes (A7).
  4. Overlay is checked before supersession, so a timed instance never ends an open-ended one of an overlay kind (A8).
  5. An applied record holds until the next one or its own end, with no staleness limit (A10): a controller that stops uploading leaves its last applied record in effect until that record ends, or indefinitely if it is open-ended.
  6. A carrier with a duration and no unit is not read (A11), rather than read in a default unit.
  7. The state version covers content (A12), so any amendment of an active instance changes it.
  8. A zero-duration record ends only an instance already running (A5). A zero-duration record written to cancel a target scheduled for later (careportal, nightguard and iAPS cancel before start this way) does not cancel it, because nothing on the record says which future instance it names.
  9. An amendment that shortens an instance is read as an early end (cancelled, A5), so an edit from 60 to 45 minutes made before the 45th minute reads the same as a cancel.
  10. Per-cycle values that name no intent give no applied instance (A10), so Trio's and iAPS's applied state is reported as composed values only.

docs.text:
path request recorded at the hub acceptance visible success visible failure visible careportal or Nocturne → Loop (hub → APNs) no no as the resulting entity Note with free text LoopFollow → Loop or Trio (direct APNs) no no reply to the sender only Note any client → iAPS (Announcement treatment) the request is the treatment no no no careportal or nightguard temporary target → Trio, AndroidAPS the request is the treatment no indistinguishable from enacted no AAPSClient → AndroidAPS (4.0.0 prereleases, Nightscout settings) yes, signed Executing Done/Ok Done/Failed, Expired, Delivery/Failed LoopCaregiver "Remote Commands 2" expects a hub collection neither hub has — — —

Neither hub forwards a reply channel in the APNs payload it builds, so a hub-routed command cannot receive a reply. Two hub writes reach no controller: Nocturne's POST /api/v4/state-spans, and a careportal or nightguard temporary target for a controller that does not download treatments.

docs.title: 8. Open
docs.text:
• The active-state choices (§6.3), for the maintainer to confirm.
  • Undeclared vocabularies (§3): for PROPOSAL-REG-CONTROLLERS to confirm with each controller's authors.
  • Effect and motivation (§5): proposed, not adopted.
  • Treatments a controller downloads and acts on (S10 treatment-download), found by the control-loop analysis: unlike a command, such an entry has no expiry, no destination, no outcome and no record that a controller acted on it (UCA-SYNC-DL-001); an edit or delete after the controller acted changes the record and not what was enacted (UCA-SYNC-DL-003).
  • Not measured: anything about AndroidAPS from data (no AndroidAPS closed-loop site in the corpus); whether shipping AndroidAPS sites turn on the NsClientAccept* preferences; Trio's preset name join; the order in which a Trio override factor and a temporary target's sensitivityRatio multiply; either hub's HTTP write path and Nocturne on PostgreSQL; xDrip+ remote and follower paths; the NightscoutKit fork LoopCaregiver uses; behaviour that depends on app lifecycle.
