docs.title: Quirks registry
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-16 at a046470cf.

A quirk is a way real Nightscout documents deviate from the schema, that enough of the ecosystem does that a reader has to handle it.

Not a bug report and not a wishlist. Each entry names a deviation, states how much of the corpus exhibits it, says which projects produce it, and says what a conforming reader should do. Prevalence is measured, not asserted: make schema-quirks replays every quirk's detector over the corpus and rewrites the measured block. An entry whose detector finds nothing is reported, not silently kept.

make schema-quirks           # measure every quirk against the corpus
make schema-quirks-check     # fail if a registry claim no longer matches

docs.title: Why a registry rather than schema changes
docs.text:
Some of these can be fixed in the schema — a declared type widened, an enum extended — and the 2025.2.0 spec revision did exactly that where it was safe. But widening a type records that two shapes exist, not why, who writes each, how common each is, or what to do with them. A reader implementing entries.date needs to know that a fractional value is normal and should be rounded, not merely that number is allowed.

The registry is also where a deviation lives when the schema should not change: a sentinel value, a case mismatch that should be normalized at the boundary, or two structurally different shapes for the same concept.

docs.title: App compatibility data format
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 127f69e16.

One file per group of apps (ios.yaml, android.yaml, uploaders.yaml, readers.yaml), read by tools/nsschema/compat_tables.py, which writes the tables in spec/compatibility.md, and checked by tools/nsschema/test_compat.py. Each entry says what an app does today with a Nightscout hub, layer by layer, and what it sees from a hub that implements the platform specifications without the app changing. Every claim is read from source at the ref named, and cites the anchor it was read from or the per-client file that holds it.

- app: LoopFollow                     # the name people use
  kind: follower                      # controller | uploader | follower | reader | hub | tool
  ref: "LoopFollow@4a74b781 (v7.1.0)" # repo@sha, and the release when there is one
  source: reports/consumer-impact-15.0.9/clients/ios/LoopFollow.md   # the per-client file read
  layers:
    L0:                               # identity: ids it sends and reads, re-sends
      verdict: unchanged              # unchanged | gains | opt-in | affected | none
      today: "Writes no records; reads _id only from the subjects reply."
      newer: "Nothing it reads changes (I2, I4)."
      rules: [I2, I4]                 # rule ids or "<spec> §N" that decide the 'newer' cell
      anchors: ["LoopFollow@4a74b781 LoopFollow/Helpers/...swift:50-65"]   # optional
    L1: {...}                         # records: collections and fields it writes and reads
    L2: {...}                         # registration: what it declares (nothing today) and how a
                                      # newer hub attributes its writes (registration §17)
    L3: {...}                         # state, intent and commands: overrides, targets, profile
                                      # switches, remote commands, plans
    L4: {...}                         # sync: API v1, API v3, the socket, paging, count
    L5: {...}                         # authority: how it authenticates, which permissions it needs,
                                      # and what changes under TENANCY_MODE=multi
  notes: "optional, one or two sentences"

Verdicts, for the newer cell:

verdict means unchanged the app behaves as today; nothing it sends or reads changes gains the app benefits without changing (a fix, a better match, attribution) opt-in a capability exists for it, which it uses only if it changes (typed writes, registration, the command record, plans) affected something it does today answers differently; the cell says what and which rule none the app does not touch this layer

docs.title: Command conformance case format
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at baa67a88f.

Cases for the commands specification §2 and §4–§7, checked by tools/nsschema/test_commands.py against the reference in tools/nsschema/commands.py. Every case is synthetic and its expectations are written by hand from the specification, not from the reference.

Routing per registration §9 is given, not computed: each instance states the channels on which it holds device command-sink, and over which interval.

# Synthetic. SPEC-REG-COMMANDS; commands §N. Times are seconds; expectations authored by hand.
id: <file stem>
title: <one line>
rules: [CM13]
description: <what it shows>
control: <another case id>          # optional: the passing counterpart of a refusal
mode: single | multi
maxExpirySeconds: 3600
instances:
  i-ctl-a:
    tenant: A
    subject: s-ctl-a
    product: ControllerA
    definitionId: sha256:d-a          # an opaque string in cases
    simulated: false                   # optional; a simulated sink is never a destination
    sinks: {override: [0, null]}       # channel: [from, until), null = still holding
    proposes: [override]               # optional: channels it holds a granted propose role on
    agent: true                        # optional, default true: its propose role is an agent's (CM14)
    cadence: {nominalSeconds: 300, maxDeferralSeconds: 60}   # optional, default {nominalSeconds: 30}: CM29
    fetchIntervalSeconds: 20           # optional: a declared fetch bound (CM29)
    liveTransports: [socket]           # optional, default none: transports it listens on for signals (CM28)
    ownTransports: [apns]              # optional: its own command paths outside the hub (CM31)
declares:                              # products declaring each channel, per tenant; none = no-command-destination
  A: {override: [ControllerA], example/slot: [ControllerA, ControllerB]}
shared: [override]                     # optional: shared channels, where §2's product inference does not apply
maxPayloadBytes: 4096                  # optional, default 4096: CM5
commandsOffered: true                  # optional, default true: false = the capability has no commands member (CM31)
liveTransports: [socket]               # optional, default [socket]: the hub's commands.liveTransports (CM28)
minFetchIntervalSeconds: 15            # optional, default 0: CM29
pushCredentials: {A: [apns]}           # optional: platform push credentials each tenant holds (CM20)
deploymentPushCredentials: [apns]      # optional: the deployment's own, which a signal never uses (CM20)
subjects:
  s-care: {tenant: A, permissions: [api:commands:create]}
  s-ctl-a: {tenant: A, permissions: []}
  s-person: {tenant: A, person: true, permissions: []}   # person: acts for the person whose therapy the tenant holds (CM14)
doseRecords:                           # optional: per tenant, product: times dose or carb records reached the hub (CM22)
  A: {ControllerA: [30]}
controllerDoses:                       # optional: per instance, times of the controller's own doses (CM23)
  i-ctl-a: [30]
stateVersions:                         # optional: per tenant, product: [[from, version], ...]
  A: {ControllerA: [[0, v1], [50, v2]]}
calls:
  - {at: 10, kind: command, tenant: A, subject: s-care, channel: override,
     product: ControllerA,             # optional
     payload: {...}, expiresAt: 600,   # expiresAt optional (absolute seconds)
     requestId: r1}                    # optional
  - {at: 11, kind: signal, bound: A, command: c1}   # a fetch-now signal; bound: null = no tenant bound
  - {at: 5, kind: discover, instance: i-ctl-a}     # the controller reads the capability document (CM31)
  - {at: 12, kind: fetch, tenant: A, subject: s-ctl-a, instance: i-ctl-a}
  - {at: 13, kind: enact, instance: i-ctl-a, command: c1,
     received: {...}}                  # optional: the payload as the controller received it
  - {at: 14, kind: report, tenant: A, subject: s-ctl-a, command: c1, state: succeeded,
     checked: {...},                   # optional: the payload whose hash the report names; default the command's
     reason: limit}                    # optional
  - {at: 15, kind: read, tenant: A, command: c1}
  - {at: 16, kind: restart, instance: i-ctl-a}                # the controller restarts (CM21)
  - {at: 17, kind: outstanding, tenant: A, subject: s-care, channel: override}   # CM24
  - {at: 18, kind: cancel, tenant: A, subject: s-care, command: c1}            # CM25
  - {at: 20, kind: propose, tenant: A, subject: s-agent, instance: i-agent, channel: override,
     product: ControllerA,             # optional
     instanceId: i-ctl-a,              # optional: the instance the proposer read (CM13)
     payload: {...}, basedOn: v1, expiresAt: 600}
  - {at: 21, kind: approve, tenant: A, subject: s-care, proposal: p1,
     approves: {...}}                  # the payload whose hash the approval names
  - {at: 22, kind: reject, tenant: A, subject: s-care, proposal: p1}
  - {at: 23, kind: withdraw, tenant: A, subject: s-agent, proposal: p1}
  - {at: 24, kind: evaluate, tenant: A, subject: s-reader, proposal: p1, note: text}
end: 100                               # optional: the time final states are read at; default the last call's
expected:
  calls:                               # one entry per call, in order
    - {status: 201, commandId: c1, state: pending, fetchWithinSeconds: 30}   # command accepted (CM30)
    - {status: 201, commandId: c2, state: pending, fetchWithinSeconds: 30,   # ... with other items outstanding (CM24)
       outstanding: {proposals: [], commands: [c1], dosesSince: []}}
    - {status: 201, commandId: c1, state: pending, fetchWithinSeconds: 360,
       mayExpireUnfetched: true}                                    # expires within the fetch bound (CM30)
    - {status: 200, proposals: [p1], commands: [c1], dosesSince: [25],      # outstanding
       destinations: {i-ctl-a: {fetchWithinSeconds: 30}}}
    - {status: 200, state: cancelled} | {status: 202, state: fetched, cancelRequested: true}  # cancel
    - {status: 409, code: no-command-destination, commandId: c2}    # refused at routing, recorded as not-routed
    - {status: 422, code: expiry-required}                          # refused, not recorded
    - {status: 200, commandId: c1, state: fetched}                  # requestId re-send: the first command
    - {signalled: true, to: i-ctl-a, via: socket, carries: {}}      # signal (CM27)
    - {signalled: false, reason: withheld | expired | nothing-waiting | no-live-transport | no-tenant-credential}
    - {hubPath: true, fetchWithinSeconds: 30, live: socket, keeps: [apns]} | {hubPath: false, keeps: [apns]}  # discover
    - {status: 200, commands: [c1]}                                 # fetch
    - {status: 200, commands: [], cancels: [c1]}                    # fetch carrying a cancel (CM25)
    - {state: succeeded} | {state: refused, reason: hash-mismatch}  # enact: the controller's check
    - {state: ignored, reason: duplicate}                           # enact: a commandId already decided (CM21)
    - {}                                                            # restart
    - {status: 200} | {status: 403, code: not-registration-owner}   # report
    - {status: 200, state: fetched} | {status: 404}                 # read
    - {status: 201, proposalId: p1}                                 # propose
    - {status: 201, commandId: c1, state: pending, fetchWithinSeconds: 30}   # approve
    - {status: 200}                                                 # reject, withdraw
    - {status: 201}                                                 # evaluate
  commands: {c1: {state: succeeded, destination: i-ctl-a, proposalId: p1}}  # at `end`
                                       # plus hashMismatch: true when a report named another hash (CM7)
                                       # and mayExpireUnfetched: true when flagged (CM30)
  proposals: {p1: {state: approved}}

Ids are assigned in order: commands c1, c2, … (accepted commands and commands refused at routing, which CM1 records), proposals p1, p2, … (accepted proposals only). destination is null for a command refused at routing. A permission or validation refusal is not recorded and gets no id.

Expiry: a command past expiresAt is never signalled or fetched, and reads report it expired unless it was fetched (unconfirmed) or an outcome came first. A fetch returns pending and fetched commands until the controller reports (CM26); a signal changes no state. With commandsOffered: false, command, propose and fetch answer 404.

docs.title: Plan conformance case format
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 7a1a09b5a.

Cases for the plans specification, rules PN1–PN16, checked by tools/nsschema/test_plans.py against the reference in tools/nsschema/plans.py. Every case is synthetic and its expectations are written by hand from the specification, not from the reference. A plan case uses everything in the command case format (instances, declares, subjects, the command, fetch, enact, report, evaluate, withdraw and reject calls), and adds:

# Synthetic. SPEC-PLANS; plans §N. Times are seconds; expectations authored by hand.
maxProposalSeconds: 1209600            # optional, default 14 days: PN1
maxPlanSeconds: 2592000                # optional, default 30 days: PN4
maxAdvanceApprovalSeconds: 43200       # optional, default 12 hours: PN13
riskClasses:                           # per product, element kind: R0-R6; undeclared is R4 (PN3)
  ControllerA: {eatingSoon: R1, mealBolus: R4, schoolOverride: R2, basalProfile: R5, maxBolus: R6}
channelVersions:                       # per tenant, product, channel: [[from, version], ...] (PN7)
  A: {ControllerA: {override: [[0, v1], [500, v2]]}}
subjects:
  s-person: {tenant: A, person: true, permissions: [api:commands:create]}    # the person (CM14, PN6)
  s-care: {tenant: A, delegate: true, permissions: [api:commands:create]}    # a delegate acting for them
  s-agent-2: {tenant: A, agent: true, permissions: [api:commands:create]}    # an agent's credential
instances:
  i-agent:
    proposesChanges: [[38, []]]               # optional: its propose roles from a time on (PN12)
  i-ctl-a:
    definitionId: sha256:d-a
    definitionChanges: [[400, sha256:d-a2]]   # optional: the instance renews under another definition
    sinks: {example/plans: [0, null]}         # the product's plan channel
calls:
  - {at: 10, kind: proposePlan, tenant: A, subject: s-agent, instance: i-agent,
     channel: example/plans, product: ControllerA, expiresAt: 5000,
     basedOn: {override: v1},          # channel -> that channel's state version
     plan:
       elements:
         - {id: soon, kind: eatingSoon, channel: override, path: standing, content: {...}}
         - {id: meal, kind: mealBolus, channel: example/bolus, path: standing, content: {...},
            standingConditions: {mitigation: reduced-portion,
                                 withdrawal: [{signal: location, evaluatedBy: controller}],
                                 companion: soon}}
       trigger: {...}                  # stored unread
       startsAt: 100
       endsAt: 100000
       requiredReviews: [risk-check]}
  - {at: 20, kind: evaluate, tenant: A, subject: s-risk, proposal: p1, review: risk-check, note: text}
  - {at: 30, kind: approvePlan, tenant: A, subject: s-person, proposal: p1,
     accepts: [{element: soon, hash: <sha256 of the element's canonical JSON>}]}
  - {at: 40, kind: report, tenant: A, subject: s-ctl-a, command: c1, state: succeeded}   # PN9
  - {at: 50, kind: confirm, tenant: A, subject: s-agent, instance: i-agent, plan: p1,
     occurrence: d1, occursAt: 3600}
  - {at: 60, kind: approveOccurrence, tenant: A, subject: s-person, plan: p1, occurrence: d1,
     occursAt: 3600, element: meal, hash: <...>}
  - {at: 70, kind: skip, tenant: A, subject: s-person, plan: p1, occurrence: d2}
  - {at: 80, kind: planReport, tenant: A, subject: s-ctl-a, plan: p1,
     occurrence: d1, occurrenceState: ran}            # or planState: ended
  - {at: 90, kind: endPlan, tenant: A, subject: s-person, plan: p1}
  - {at: 91, kind: outstanding, tenant: A, subject: s-follower, channel: example/bolus}   # PN18
  - {at: 92, kind: cancel, tenant: A, subject: s-person, command: c4}                    # CM25
  - {at: 95, kind: readPlan, tenant: A, subject: s-follower, plan: p1}
expected:
  calls:
    - {status: 201, proposalId: p1}                                   # proposePlan
    - {status: 201, commandId: c1, state: pending}                    # approvePlan, confirm,
                                                                      # approveOccurrence, skip, endPlan
    - {status: 200}                                                   # planReport
    - {status: 200, state: active, accepted: [soon], declined: [meal],
       occurrences: {d1: ran}}                                        # readPlan
    - {status: 422, code: standing-conditions-required}               # a refusal
  commands: {c1: {state: fetched, destination: i-ctl-a}}              # at `end`
  proposals: {p1: {state: approved}}
  plans: {p1: {state: active, accepted: [soon], declined: [meal], occurrences: {d1: ran}}}

The plan id is the proposal id. Element hashes: write hash: element:<id> to mean "the hash of element <id> of the plan as proposed", and hash: wrong for any other value; the test resolves element:<id> before replaying the calls, so expectations never carry computed hashes. Command ids are assigned in order across every call that creates one, as in the command format. The mirror (plans:) is listed for every approved plan at end. declined lists the plan's element ids that the approval did not name, in the plan's order.

docs.title: AAPS Profile-Edit Emission Audit
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-04-20 at 3136d34a7.

Goal: enumerate exactly what AAPS uploads to Nightscout when a user edits the Local Profile and presses Save, separately for NSClient (V1) and NSClientV3.

References use commit-stable paths under externals/AndroidAPS/.

docs.title: Triggering action
docs.text:
ProfileFragment "Save" button:

plugins/main/src/main/kotlin/app/aaps/plugins/main/profile/ProfileFragment.kt:338-348

binding.save.setOnClickListener {
  ...
  profilePlugin.storeSettings(activity, dateUtil.now())
}

ProfilePlugin.storeSettings (plugins/main/.../ProfilePlugin.kt:184-209):

  1. Persists profile fields to local preferences.
  2. Sets LongNonKey.LocalProfileLastChange = timestamp (i.e. now()).
  3. Calls createAndStoreConvertedProfile().
  4. rxBus.send(EventProfileStoreChanged()).

Crucially, no ProfileSwitch treatment is created here. createProfileSwitch (implementation/.../ProfileFunctionImpl.kt:167-197) is invoked only from:

  • ProfileSwitchDialog (user-initiated switch)
  • loadFromStore flow (when receiving from NS) — indirectly via callers
  • The keep-alive worker re-sending an existing switch

So a Local Profile edit by itself emits only the profile-store update, not a profile-switch.

docs.title: animations — figures that change over time, drawn from data
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 8904a2a95.

Contributor-facing. One manim scene, drawn from the same files as the static rule figures, rendered into docs/30-design/platform/animations/ as a VP9 .webm (1280×720, 30 fps), a poster .png (the last frame) and a .sources.json sidecar.

make animations          # render (needs manim 0.20 and PyAV; MANIM_PY, MANIM, ANIM_MEDIA)
make animations-check    # fail naming each animation whose scene or inputs changed since its render

make animations runs render.py --media-dir $(ANIM_MEDIA). manim writes its cache and a lossless QuickTime RLE render there, outside the repository; render.py encodes VP9 once (crf 32), renders the poster with manim -s, writes the sidecar, and refuses a video over 2 MB or a set over 10 MB.

Animation · scene Shows Source Grade Static figure active-state-spans · active_state_spans.py ActiveStateSpans rules A5–A8 of state and intent §6.1, one case each: records land in the order the hub received them, the derived instances start, end, are superseded or vanish as each lands, then a cursor visits each "active at" query; the last frame lists each case's instances and active sets specs/sync/conformance/active-state/ (loaded with tools/diagrams/active_state_rules.py); instances after each record from tools/nsschema/active_state.py; rule names from spec/state-intent.md synthetic cases; after the last record the instances equal each case's expected block, or the scene refuses to render diagrams/active-state-a5.svg … a8.svg

Text size. The site shows the 1280 px video 688 px wide on a 1440 px desktop window and 358 px wide on a 390 px phone (measured in headless Chrome, 2026-10-18), a scale of 0.54 and 0.28. Text is manim font size 18 or more (common.MIN_SIZE; a 22.5 px CSS font on the canvas), which shows at 12.1 px on the desktop and 6.3 px on the phone; the per-case frames use 20 (13.4 px on the desktop). On a phone the poster and the static figures diagrams/active-state-a5.svg … a8.svg carry the content. Two earlier scenes were replaced by static figures on 2026-10-18 because their text showed at 9.4 px on the desktop: the two hubs' readings (hub-active-state; the static diagrams/hub-active-state-*.svg show every case) and the command lifecycle, whose call lines with payload, hash and expiry do not fit four lanes at font size 18 (tools/diagrams/command_lifecycle.py draws it).

sources.py lists each animation's scene, class and inputs; the scenes import their case lists from it. An input is a file, hashed whole, or a specification with the rule ids whose bold names the animation shows: only those names are hashed, so other edits to the specification do not make the animation stale.

test_animations.py: video bytes are not deterministic, so the drift test compares the sidecar's hashes with the files as they stand; it also checks the poster, sidecar and sizes. Its controls each change one input in a temporary copy (an active-state case, a rule name in state-intent.md, the scene file, common.py) and require that the animation is reported stale; an edit to state-intent.md outside the rule names, or to a lab result no animation draws, must report none.

Rules the scenes keep, as tools/diagrams does: data only (every instance and active set comes from a case or a reference function the cases are tested against); text at manim font size 18 or more; the tools/diagrams palette; roles and products only, no people or companies; calm motion, about 1.5 s on each state change; a final frame that summarises and serves as the poster.

docs.title: 📊 CGMENCODE: CGM/Insulin Representation Learning Pipeline
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-06-27 at d51fff093.

The Bridge from Physics Simulation to Artificial Intelligence.

This package turns physics-simulated and real-world glucose-insulin data into neural network training vectors. It is the foundation for building a Physiological Digital Twin that can predict glucose outcomes and evaluate dosing safety.

Provenance: Imported from t1pal-mobile-workspace/tools/cgmencode/ (2026-03-31). This is R&D-phase code brought into the ecosystem alignment workspace to compose with the physics simulation (cgmsim-lib/UVA-Padova), algorithm validation (aid-autoresearch), and conformance vector infrastructure that already live here. When the approach stabilizes, it may be spun out into its own repository.

docs.title: 1. Environment Setup
docs.text:
cd tools/cgmencode
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: 2. Generate Training Data (Physics → Vectors)
docs.text:
# Generate 50-patient Latin Hypercube sweep using cgmsim engine
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.generate_training_data \
  --patients 50 --engine cgmsim --output-dir externals/sweep-data

# Or use UVA/Padova physiological engine
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.generate_training_data \
  --patients 50 --engine uva-padova --output-dir externals/sweep-uva

docs.title: 3. Train a Model
docs.text:
# Train the Transformer AE (recommended starting point)
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.train --model ae --epochs 50 \
  --data externals/sweep-uva

# Train the Conditioned Transformer (dosing "what-if")
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.train --model conditioned --epochs 50 \
  --data externals/sweep-uva

docs.title: 4. Evaluate
docs.text:
# Evaluate against persistence baseline
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.evaluate --model ae \
  --checkpoint checkpoints/ae_best.pt --data externals/sweep-uva

# Test the real-data adapter (self-test with synthetic trace)
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.real_data_adapter --test

docs.title: 5. Legacy Commands (from original fixtures)
docs.text:
# These require Nightscout algorithm-replay fixtures in fixtures/ — 
# use the sim_adapter or generate_training_data workflows above instead.
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.model          # Basic AE on fixture data
python3 -m tools.cgmencode.toolbox vae 5  # Experimental architectures

docs.title: CGMENCODE Schema
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-03-31 at fe250dc86.

This document defines the schema for transforming T1Pal algorithm test fixtures into neural network training vectors.

docs.title: Feature Indices
docs.text:
The encoder produces a 3D NumPy array of shape (Samples, TimeSteps, Features).

Index Feature Type Description 0 glucose Input/State Sensor Glucose Value (mg/dL). Primary target for forecasting. 1 iob Input/State Insulin on Board (Units). Represents active insulin in the body. 2 cob Input/State Carbs on Board (Grams). Represents unabsorbed carbohydrates. 3 net_basal Action Temp Basal Rate relative to scheduled basal (U/hr). 4 bolus Action Discrete insulin doses, including SMBs (Units). 5 carbs Action Discrete carbohydrate entries (Grams). 6 time_sin Temporal sin(2π · hour/24). Encodes circadian position on unit circle. 7 time_cos Temporal cos(2π · hour/24). Paired with time_sin so 23:55 ≈ 00:05.

docs.title: 1. PhenotypeFactsLoader (320 lines)
docs.text:
File: production/phenotype_facts_loader.py

What it does: Merges 3 independent phenotype experiments into one lazy-loaded cache.

from tools.cgmencode.production.phenotype_facts_loader import PhenotypeFactsLoader

loader = PhenotypeFactsLoader()

# Lookup patient phenotype (thread-safe, cached)
facts = loader.lookup('patient-id-xyz')

# Returns frozen dataclass with all 6 orthogonal axes:
facts.stack_score              # Evening bolus stacking (EXP-2882)
facts.brake_ratio              # Basal suspension % (EXP-2885)
facts.counter_reg_intercept    # Recovery intercept (EXP-2877)
facts.beta_nadir               # Dose-response slope (EXP-2878)
facts.p_haaf                   # HAAF fragility p-value (counterfactual, EXP-2878)
facts.evening_bolus_excess_4h  # 4h cumulative bolus excess (EXP-2881)
facts.controller_lineage       # "Loop" | "oref0" | "Trio" (EXP-2885)

# Coverage reporting
coverage = loader.coverage_by_axis()
# {'stack_score': 25/27 patients, 'brake_ratio': 27/27, ...}

Key Design Principle: All 6 axes kept orthogonal (|ρ| < 0.32) - ❌ DON'T composite them: risk = stack * (1-brake) * recovery - ✅ DO use them separately for stratification/audition

Why this matters: Compositing loses -0.227 adj-R² (observed -0.019 vs orthogonal +0.208)

Example from audition: 

class AuditionInputs:
    phenotype = PhenotypeFactsLoader()

    def hypo_risk_factors(self, patient_id: str):
        facts = self.phenotype.lookup(patient_id)

        if facts is None:
            return {"risk": "unknown"}

        # Separate signals = better deconfounding
        return {
            "bolus_stacking": facts.stack_score,
            "suspension_aggressive": facts.brake_ratio < 0.08,
            "fragile_to_depth": facts.beta_nadir > 0.5,
            "haaf_risk": facts.p_haaf < 0.05,
        }

docs.title: 2. TreatmentDedupFactsLoader (250 lines)
docs.text:
File: production/treatment_dedup_facts_loader.py

What it does: Provides per-patient treatment deduplication strategy with confidence scoring.

from tools.cgmencode.production.treatment_dedup_facts_loader import (
    TreatmentDedupFactsLoader,
)

loader = TreatmentDedupFactsLoader()

# Lookup patient dedup strategy
strategy = loader.lookup('patient-id-xyz')

# Returns frozen dataclass with dedup parameters:
strategy.dedup_window_sec       # Time window for merge (e.g., 60 sec)
strategy.tie_breaker_priority   # ["sync_id", "timestamp", "amount"] ordered
strategy.use_sync_id            # Boolean: weight sync IDs in dedup
strategy.sync_id_field          # "syncIdentifier" or "nightscoutId"
strategy.event_type_confidence  # {"bolus": 0.95, "carbs": 0.80, ...}
strategy.confidence             # Overall dedup confidence (0.0-1.0)

Example from audition: 

def deduplicate_treatments(self, patient_id: str, treatments: list) -> list:
    strategy = TreatmentDedupFactsLoader().lookup(patient_id)

    if strategy is None:
        # Graceful degradation: use conservative defaults
        strategy = TreatmentDedupFactsLoader()._default_strategy()

    # Apply strategy
    deduped = []
    for i, t1 in enumerate(treatments):
        if any(self._is_duplicate(t1, t2, strategy) for t2 in deduped):
            continue
        deduped.append(t1)

    return deduped

docs.title: 📋 CGMENCODE: Engineering & Research Roadmap
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-03-31 at fe250dc86.

This document outlines the roadmap for moving from a prototype toolbox to a production-grade physiological modeling system.

Last Updated: 2026-04 (after physics→ML bridge, sweep training, and UVA/Padova validation)

docs.title: Phase 1: Data Acquisition (Scaling the Dataset) — ✅ DONE
docs.text:
Goal: Move from ~1,000 vectors to 10,000+ vectors.

  • SIM-* → cgmencode bridge (sim_adapter.py): Converts physics simulation output to 8-feature training vectors. Handles both SIM- and TV- conformance formats.
  • Latin Hypercube parameter sweep (generate_training_data.py): Generates diverse patient profiles (ISF 15–80, CR 5–20, basal 0.3–3.0, weight 45–110, DIA 4–8) via LHS sampling.
  • Patient parameter CLI (in-silico-bridge.js): Added --isf, --cr, --basal-rate, --weight, --dia, --patient, --id-prefix, --output-dir flags.
  • Multi-engine support: Both cgmsim and UVA/Padova engines produce training data via --engine flag.
  • Scaled to 50 patients: 3,500 cgmsim vectors + 2,400 UVA/Padova vectors generated.
  • Real patient data: real_data_adapter.py built and tested with synthetic trace. Blocked on OhioT1DM dataset download from PhysioNet (credentialed access required).
  • ~~Automate Nightscout History Ingestion~~: Deferred — physics sweep provides sufficient volume for current R&D.

docs.title: diagrams — figures drawn from data
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 8904a2a95.

Contributor-facing. Generates the SVG figures under docs/30-design/platform/diagrams/ from the files that hold the facts they show, so a figure changes only when its source does. Pure Python (PyYAML); same card, font and text measure as tools/structure-diagrams.

make diagrams-svg          # regenerate every figure
make diagrams-svg-check    # fail naming each committed figure that differs from its sources
Module · function Figures Source Grade hub_active_state.py · figure() hub-active-state-treatments.svg, hub-active-state-devicestatus-profile.svg tools/lab/hub-active-state/records/cases.json, results/crm.json, results/nocturne.json, results/RESULTS.md (run date and commits) measured end_encoding.py · figure() end-encoding-loop.svg, end-encoding-trio.svg, end-encoding-androidaps.svg specs/sync/registrations/{loop,trio,androidaps}.yaml, stateSpans read-derived active_state_rules.py · figure() active-state-a3.svg … active-state-a9.svg, active-state-a13.svg specs/sync/conformance/active-state/*.yaml (the cases' records and expected blocks); the rule's name and sentence from docs/30-design/platform/spec/state-intent.md §6.1 synthetic cases command_lifecycle.py · figure() command-lifecycle.svg specs/sync/conformance/commands/ (five cases: calls and expected blocks, replayed by tools/nsschema/commands.py); rule names from docs/30-design/platform/spec/commands.md proposed, synthetic cases

build.py collects every module's build() ({file name: SVG text}) and writes them; --check compares instead. Each module's docstring says what each mark means.

Rules the generators keep:

  • Data only. A figure draws what its source states. The rule figures draw each case's expected answer and apply no rule themselves; active_state_rules.RULES lists the cases drawn per rule, and build() refuses a case that neither cites the rule nor is the control of a drawn case that does.
  • Deterministic. No timestamps or random ids; every coordinate goes through svgkit.num().
  • Legible at the site's width. Drawn 720 px wide, text at 12 px or more. The site shows a figure 688 px wide on a 1440 px desktop window (measured in headless Chrome, 2026-10-18), so 12 px text shows at 11.5 px; command-lifecycle.svg uses 13 px or more (12.4 px shown). svgkit.svg() refuses a figure with text measured past the card edge.
  • Accessible. Each SVG carries <title> and <desc>; the desc states the figure's finding from the data. A state is never colour alone: a disagreement cell is red and marked ≠, a deletion is a cross, an end reason is written out.
  • Roles and products only. Controller and hub product names; no people or companies.

test_diagrams.py: the staleness test regenerates every figure and compares it with the committed file; five controls each change one input in a temporary copy (a lab answer, a registration's endedEncoding, a case's expected end, a command case's call time, a rule name in commands.md) and require that exactly the figure drawn from it is reported stale. A change to a rule's wording in state-intent.md §6.1 makes that rule's figure stale too: run make diagrams-svg after editing it.

docs.title: aaps-ws-delivery lab (BF-164)
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-25 at b1ec05bca.

When does a record written outside API v3 reach a client that behaves like AndroidAPS NSClientV3 in websocket mode? Built for the AndroidAPS websocket delivery note and register BF-164.

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only. Two lab servers on 127.0.0.1, each with its own database; never point it at a real site.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
# MongoDB on 127.0.0.1:27316 (any version the tree supports), and an installed tree
tools/lab/aaps-ws-delivery/start-servers.sh <crm worktree> <outdir> [mongodb://127.0.0.1:27316]
node tools/lab/aaps-ws-delivery/aaps-ws-lab.js <crm worktree> <outdir>
# stop: kill the PIDs in <outdir>/source.pid and <outdir>/target.pid
  • start-servers.sh boots a source Nightscout (port 17317, database bf164src) and the target under test (port 17316, database bf164tgt) with nightscout-connect reading the source (CONNECT_SOURCE=nightscout), so connector writes are real. Both use AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied. Two API secrets are generated per run into <outdir>/secrets (mode 600); nothing secret lives in this directory.
  • aaps-ws-lab.js creates a follower subject with the built-in readable role and a writer subject with admin, then runs the scenarios below with a simulated client (SimAAPS). Each modelling choice cites the AndroidAPS file it comes from (comments C1 to C7 at the top of the script). Liveness of both servers is checked around every measured step. Output: <outdir>/lab.log and <outdir>/results.json.

Scenarios, for a carb written through API v1, through the main socket (dbAdd), and a reading written by nightscout-connect: S1 the socket stays up for 45 s; S2 a reconnect with no API v3 write in that collection in between; S3 a reconnect after an API v3 write in the same collection. Control: an API v3 create while the socket is up.

Results: results/2026-10-25-dev-b29f1bf7/ (dev b29f1bf7, Node v22.23.4). The connector's copy took 84 to 190 s in that run, so a full run takes about 7.5 min.

docs.title: bf94-browser — BF-94 in a real browser
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-02 at b853ac127.

Contributor-facing. Measures whether an open Nightscout page keeps showing a temp basal that has been shortened or cancelled (register BF-94, queue BFQ-94). Synthetic data only.

  • probe.js boots one cgm-remote-monitor tree on a fresh database, seeds a 1.0 U/h profile and CGM readings, uploads a 2.0 U/h temp, opens the page in Chromium (Playwright), makes one scenario's change over REST as the client does, then samples the open page every 2 s: the basal pill's text and the basal line's value at "now" read from the rendered SVG. A fresh page in a new browser context and a reload of the open page are the control. The header comment describes the options.
  • run-all.sh <label> <tree> <port> <outdir> runs every scenario with and without earlier temps on the chart. It needs NODE_PATH pointing at a node_modules with playwright, and a MongoDB 7 at 127.0.0.1:27941 started with --ulimit nofile=64000:64000.

Scenarios: loop-new (a new temp), trio-reupload-new (the old temp re-uploaded shortened, then a new one), aaps-v3 (PATCH the old temp shorter, POST a new one), cancel-trio, cancel-aaps-v3, cancel-oref (a zero-length temp).

docs.title: brush-extent — BF-168 in a real browser
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-07 at 4e7694d02.

Contributor-facing. Measures whether the context chart's window (the brush under the main chart) can be dragged back to now (register BF-168, queue BFQ-168). Synthetic data only.

  • probe.js boots one cgm-remote-monitor tree on a fresh database, seeds a profile and 48 h of CGM readings, opens the main page in Chromium (Playwright) and records the brush's drag limit (d3-brush's stored extent) beside the context chart's width. Then it taps the middle of the context chart, drags the window to the right edge, drags again from near the edge and taps inside the right edge, recording retro mode and the brush selection after each step. The header comment describes the modes; -force makes every <svg> report the browser default 300x150 for 6 s after load, which is the race made certain.

It needs NODE_PATH pointing at a node_modules with playwright, n with Node 22.23.2, and a MongoDB (the runs below used a dedicated mongo:7.0.43 container).

docs.title: Results, 2026-10-07
docs.text:
Trees: dev 43289dde, v15.0.8 92d08342, and the fix branch bf/brush-extent b919af9f (one commit on dev 43289dde). Chromium 1243 under Playwright 1.56.1, Node 22.23.2.

Forced (results/*-force*.json):

tree mode drag limit at load after dragging right dev touch 300 (chart 884) stuck at [245, 300], retro, about 1900 min behind now v15.0.8 touch 300 (chart 884) stuck at [245, 300], retro, about 1900 min behind now fix touch, mouse, touch after rotating the chart's width [829, 884] / [1196, 1276], at now

The tap inside the right edge did not bring dev or v15.0.8 back to now in the forced run.

Unforced (results/unforced-runs.json; these drags ended 40 px past the chart edge): the drag limit at load was 300 while the chart was 406 or 872 px wide in 3 of 28 loads, once on dev and twice on v15.0.8. Both v15.0.8 cases were phone loads with no resize afterwards, and the drag stopped at x = 300 (2 of 12 such loads on v15.0.8; 0 of 11 on dev). The dev case was followed by a resize, which re-reads the limit (window.onresize reaches updateBrushToNow(), which calls the brush again), and the drag then reached now.

Fix, unforced (results/fix[1-5]-touch.json, fix-mouse-widen.json): 5 of 5 phone loads and the widened desktop load reached now.

Mechanism, read from the code and confirmed by the runs: chart.charts is the <g> inside the <svg>, so chart.charts.attr('width', …) never sizes the <svg>; d3-brush's default extent reads the <svg>'s own size when .call(chart.brush) runs, and chart.update() never calls the brush again when the width changes.

docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-25 at b1ec05bca.

Which MongoDB servers a cgm-remote-monitor tree boots and passes its integration tier against, and what an operator sees when the driver refuses the server. Built for the MongoDB server compatibility matrix note (2026-10-25: dev b29f1bf7 with driver 5.9.2, cut 3 with driver 7.7.0, servers 3.6 to 8.0).

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only: each cell uses its own database on a lab container and must never be pointed at a real site.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
1. Start one container per server, named mm-mongo-<suffix>, from the official mongo images, each published on its own host port (the 2026-10-25 run used 27450 to 27457 for suffixes 36, 40, 42, 44, 50, 60, 70 and 80). Read buildInfo from each before labelling a run.
  2. Install each tree with npm ci (the tier runner and the server need its node_modules).
  3. Boot cells, one at a time:
MM_OUT=/path/to/out tools/lab/mongo-server-matrix/boot.sh <tree> dev-42 27452 31502 60
  1. Integration cells, one container each (several may run at once, since each cell shares only its own container's network namespace):
MM_OUT=/path/to/out tools/lab/mongo-server-matrix/run-tree.sh <tree> dev 36 40 42 44 50 60 70 80
variable default meaning MM_OUT $TMPDIR/mongo-server-matrix logs, generated env files, results MM_GITDIR externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official/.git mounted read-only into the test container MM_NODE unset (the node:22 image's own) a host node binary to mount instead

boot.sh generates the API secret per run. itest-docker.sh uses the tree's own tests/ci.test.env with only the connection string changed. Nothing secret lives in this directory.

Contributor-facing. Compares, operation by operation, the v1 and v3 API that cgm-remote-monitor documents for 16.0.0 with what Nocturne documents and serves on the same paths. Two parts: a diff of the two projects' OpenAPI documents, and one probe set run unchanged against both servers, booted from pinned commits, with synthetic data only. Feeds the Nocturne row of the compatibility specification (docs/30-design/platform/spec/compatibility.md) and the HUB-REG-NOCTURNE packet.

Result: results/compare.md (generated; the machine-readable inputs sit beside it).

commit what cgm-remote-monitor d46ef808 head of pull request #8858: dev c08cbe03 plus accurate lib/server/swagger.yaml (v1) and lib/api3/swagger.yaml (v3); the repository's copies are specs/openapi/upstream/cgm-remote-monitor/api-v{1,3}.yaml Nocturne 89dcaf1dd main, 2026-10-26

Both are in PINS; run.sh refuses any other commit. Nocturne file:line references below are at 89dcaf1dd under src/API/Nocturne.API/ (or the path given) and are read, not run, unless a result file is named; api-v1.yaml:N and api-v3.yaml:N are lines of the repository's copies of

docs.title: What it measures
docs.text:
1. Documents. cgm-remote-monitor's two documents against Nocturne's nightscout document (its v1–v3 surface; Nocturne builds it at run time and serves it at /openapi/nightscout.json, saved as results/nocturne-nightscout-openapi.json). The build-time NSwag document (src/API/Nocturne.API/nswag.json) is the nocturne (V4) document, so it is not the one used. Each operation is classed same, differs (with the aspects: query parameters, auth schemes, response codes, 2xx body kind, 2xx body keys or record fields), only-crm or only-noc. Nocturne operations outside the paths cgm-remote-monitor's two documents cover (/api/v2/..., /pebble) are listed but not compared: cgm-remote-monitor serves v2 too, but #8858 does not document it.
  2. Behaviour. probe.js against each server (381 result lines per run on cgm-remote-monitor, 351 on Nocturne, which issues no credential for the other 30), without a credential and with a full-access one, in two anonymous-access set-ups per server (below). Each response is reduced to status, content type, body shape (kind, top-level keys, the kind of an envelope's result, record field names, array length) and, for the semantic probes, named values computed from the body (sem). Probes cover every operation in both documents that the audit for #8858 probed, plus the semantics listed under "Semantics probed".

docs.title: Path normalisation
docs.text:
Written out in ops.js, applied to both documents before operations are joined:

  1. the server URL (or a path-level servers override, as for /api/versions) is prefixed;
  2. trailing slashes are dropped;
  3. literal segments are lower-cased (both servers route case-insensitively; Nocturne's document spells controller names, /api/v1/Entries);
  4. every path parameter becomes {} whatever its name ({id}, {_id}, {spec}, {identifier});
  5. cgm-remote-monitor's v3 {collection} is expanded to its six collections;
  6. cgm-remote-monitor documents an express optional tail as one template whose description says trailing parameters may be left off (/slice/{storage}/{field}/{type}/{prefix}/{regex} is express /slice/:storage/:field{/:type}{/:prefix}{/:regex}); it is expanded to one key per depth (/slice/{}/{} … /slice/{}/{}/{}/{}/{}; /times, /times/echo and /echo likewise). Nocturne's document lists each depth as its own path;
  7. keys join exactly first; a leftover Nocturne key joins the one cgm-remote-monitor template that covers it (/api/v1/Count/entries/where joins /count/{storage}/where), never the reverse (/api/v1/Profile/{id} does not join /profile/current).

Format suffixes (/entries.json) are not part of a key; probes with a suffix are counted under the operation without it.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
• cgm-remote-monitor: API_SECRET is a random value per run. The full-access credential is its SHA-1 in api-secret. For v3, which takes a JWT (the document's only scheme), the probe mints a subject with role admin and one with readable through /api/v2/authorization/subjects and exchanges their access tokens at /api/v2/authorization/request/{token}.
  • Nocturne: there is no API_SECRET setting. setup-nocturne.js seeds one tenant with no sample data through the dev-only endpoint, signs in as its owner, and mints a direct grant with scope * (POST /api/auth/direct-grants). Nocturne stores the SHA-1 of the grant's token as a legacy secret hash (Services/Auth/DirectGrantService.cs:175, read, not run), so the token works as a site's API secret: the same SHA-1-in-api-secret request authenticates on v1 and v3 (measured). The /api/v2/authorization/subjects reply carries an empty accessToken (measured), so no JWT or read-only credential is issued, and the probes that need one are not run on Nocturne (30 per set-up).
  • The probe uses, for v3, the first of {JWT, api-secret} that /api/v3/status accepts: the JWT on cgm-remote-monitor, api-secret on Nocturne (result v3.credential). Probe results are joined on probe id and credential class (none, full, readonly, or the spelling under test), so v3 full means each server's documented full-access credential.

docs.title: Anonymous access set-ups
docs.text:
set-up cgm-remote-monitor Nocturne 1 AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied the tenant's Public member as seeded: no permissions, 24-hour clamp on 2 AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=readable Public given every read scope it accepts (Scope.PublicShareScopes), clamp off

Nocturne has no site-wide default role for requests without a credential. Read, not run: the Public member's permissions apply only to requests on a share-link host (Middleware/AuthenticationMiddleware.cs:225-227, context.IsShareAccess()), and requests to the apex go without them. Measured: set-up 2 answers anonymous apex requests exactly as set-up 1 (401 on every data read). Share-link hosts are a different URL shape and are not probed.

docs.title: object-id lab
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-25 at a3134a344.

Replays the ways real clients send, find, edit and delete a record by its own _id against several Nightscout builds side by side, and records what each build does. Built for PR nightscout/cgm-remote-monitor#8758 (bf/object-id-crud, records keep their own _id), and for anything that later touches the same paths.

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only: the lab seeds its own records and must never be pointed at a real site. Not medical advice.

Latest results: results/object-id-2026-09-25.md.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
tools/lab/object-id/lab.sh up      # mongo:7 in docker on 127.0.0.1:27181, then every build
tools/lab/object-id/lab.sh run     # probes.js against each build, then a cell-by-cell table
tools/lab/object-id/lab.sh down    # stop the builds, remove the container
variable default meaning OID_BUILDS a=externals/work/crm-6a-replay-a:3971 b=…crm-6a-replay-b:3972 d=…crm-bf-object-id-crud:3973 NAME=worktree:port, space separated. Each worktree needs npm ci done OID_STATE $TMPDIR/object-id-lab logs, per-build JSON output, and the generated API secret OID_MONGO_PORT 27181 host port for the lab's mongod OID_MONGO_IMAGE mongo:7 OID_NODE 22.23.2 Node version, through n exec OID_PROBES all comma-separated probe names (P-ID-10,P-ID-11) to run only those; P-ID-0 always runs

The API secret is generated per lab into $OID_STATE/secret; nothing secret lives in this directory. Each build gets its own database, oidlab_<NAME>, dropped by up. Every probe uses fresh random ids, so run can be repeated without up.

To test a candidate fix, add it as another build, e.g. OID_BUILDS="d=…/crm-bf-object-id-crud:3973 f=…/my-fix:3975". To ablate, make a scratch git worktree add of the head, revert one file, symlink node_modules, and add it as a build (the 2026-09-24 results show one, build r).

docs.title: proxy-trust lab
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-02 at 79cbc140c.

Measures how Nightscout (cgm-remote-monitor) resolves the client address (lib/server/client-ip.js / getRemoteIP) and how the failed-login delay (lib/authorization/delaylist.js) behaves, behind real proxy software and real sockets, under each TRUST_PROXY setting. Built for PR nightscout/cgm-remote-monitor#8754 (branch bf2/auth-hardening).

All numbers here were reproduced live on 2026-09-24 against:

tree branch SHA dev baseline dev f1591069 PR (TRUST_PROXY) bf2/auth-hardening 81623f9b (PR head 280eccbe is this + a dev merge; lib/server/client-ip.js is byte-identical) delay-order revert (O4b; O2 across all header families) bf2/auth-delay-dev-order f6f361b1 (lib/server/client-ip.js identical to 81623f9b and unchanged at 607d51b0)

docs.title: What TRUST_PROXY does (from the code under test)
docs.text:
lib/server/client-ip.js compiles TRUST_PROXY into how the address is resolved:

  • unset / empty (default = compatibility): address comes from the forwarded-for npm package exactly as dev does today. It reads several header families and takes the left-most entry. This is header-derived with no proxy trust boundary.
  • false: socket peer only (ignores all forwarding headers).
  • integer n: Express hop count — trust the n proxies closest to Nightscout; the address is the entry the n-th proxy saw.
  • IP / CIDR list: proxy-addr, trusting only those proxy addresses.
  • true: Express trust-all — the left-most entry.

The failed-auth delay keys on the resolved address and on a salted hash of the credential (AUTH_FAIL_DELAY ms, default 5000). It is therefore only as good as the address, which is only as good as TRUST_PROXY.

docs.title: proxy-trust lab: auth_request chain (AR) topologies
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-02 at 79cbc140c.

Add-on to this lab (lab.sh, run_matrix.sh). It does not modify either file. It covers a shape the F/TLS/L-B topologies do not: a multi-tenant hosted platform where nginx picks the next hop for each request from an auth_request subrequest, several times in a row. The shape looks like this:

client ─► L4 LB ──PROXY protocol──► GATEWAY ──► ROUTER ──► TENANT ROUTER ──► Nightscout
          (TCP)                     auth_request auth_request auth_request
                                    name→origin  name→tenant  tenant→host:port

This add-on follows the disclosure rule in README.md: mechanism, not recipe.

docs.title: Why this shape needs its own cells
docs.text:
• The hop count changes with the route. The gateway's authorizer returns the upstream origin, so one gateway can send one public name through a second router (3 HTTP hops to Nightscout) and another name straight to the tenant router (2 hops). A single TRUST_PROXY value has to be right for every route that reaches the same Nightscout.
  • The edge overwrites X-Forwarded-For. It does not append. The gateway sets X-Forwarded-For $proxy_protocol_addr and does not use real_ip. Every other lab topology appends.
  • The last hop does not set X-Forwarded-Proto. The tenant router leaves it out, so the scheme Nightscout sees is whatever the first HTTP hop wrote.
  • The backend comes from a variable. It is a header from the subrequest (proxy_pass $tenant$request_uri), so the routing itself is part of what is being tested.

docs.title: Why sockets need their own cells
docs.text:
Nightscout's socket server resolves the client address of socket.request, the socket.io handshake request. It uses the same helper as HTTP: forwarded-for on 15.0.x and dev, and lib/server/client-ip.js on #8754. A socket authorize event with a wrong secret goes through authorization.resolve(). That makes it subject to the same failed-auth delay as HTTP, and it produces the same admin-notify that the lab reads back. Three things could still differ from HTTP:

  • The handshake request depends on the transport.
  • With polling then websocket (socket.io's default, used by native clients), it is the first long-poll GET.
  • The Nightscout web client never upgrades. lib/client/index.js connects both the main and the /alarm namespaces with transports: ["polling"] (15.0.5 through dev 7000eb18). So every browser socket, including alarm acks, is a series of HTTP long-polls through every hop. The polling cells in W1, W2 and W3 are the browser's case.
  • With websocket alone, it is the Upgrade request.
  • A hop can pass HTTP but break the upgrade. It might drop Upgrade or Connection, or not speak HTTP/1.1 upstream. When that happens, the client quietly stays on polling. Any "the socket path is fine" result then describes polling, not WebSocket.
  • Upgraded and long-poll connections stay open. Hop timeouts that are harmless for REST requests can cut them off.

docs.title: rc-soak: A/B soak harness for a Nightscout release candidate
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-09-27 at 7081a144c.

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only: never point this at a real site. Nothing here is medical advice.

The harness runs two copies of Nightscout (cgm-remote-monitor) side by side, arm A and arm B, each with its own server process and its own MongoDB container, and sends both the same synthetic traffic at the same moment. It then checks that both arms stayed up, answered the same way (except where the release notes say they should differ), stored the same records, and did not grow in memory or slow down. The usual pairing is A = the shipping release, B = the release candidate.

file what it does lab.sh starts and stops everything, runs a proof or a long soak, records every PID it starts traffic.js the synthetic household: CGM uploader, Loop / Trio, AndroidAPS (API v3), followers, a web page over socket.io, edits and deletes sampler.js every 10 s (60 s real-time): is each server alive, answering, and serving the newest reading; RSS, open files, document counts from MongoDB preload.js loaded into each server with NODE_OPTIONS=--require (the build is not modified): heap, RSS, event-loop delay every 10 s proxy.js fault injection only: a proxy that silently drops a fraction of devicestatus uploads fake-apns.js a local stand-in for Apple's push service, one per arm, counting the HTTP/2 sessions each server leaves open analyze.js turns a run directory into a verdict: PASS, FAIL (findings) or INVALID probe-deleted-entry.js a one-shot check against one server: is a reading deleted by _id still returned by GET /api/v1/entries.json?count=10? probe-v3-late-mills.js BF-146: boots a tree's server on its own test database; do a bolus, carbs and a device status written through API v3 with a time in the past count in IOB and COB and take their place in GET /api/v1/devicestatus.json, as v1 writes do? expected-diffs.json the differences 15.0.9 makes on purpose, each tied to a release-notes section; thresholds

traffic.js, sampler.js, proxy.js and analyze.js adapt the connector soak lab (tools/lab/connector-soak/: writer, sampler, proxy, analyser, disturbances). The request shapes follow the client surveys in tools/lab/object-id/probes.js and reports/consumer-impact-15.0.9/lab-results.md.

docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-08. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing. Snapshot of run 023, made 2026-10-08 starting 04:17Z: the full suite in six cells, run 022's probes (re-run or carried with the client-only rationale below), the browser hand-check gate, and the compressed A/B soak with harness 5 in tools/lab/rc-soak/. expected-diffs.json was not changed. Synthetic data only, de-identified. The soak's run directories (requests, ledgers, samples, server logs and generated secrets) stay outside version control; the reports, probe logs, gate output and suite logs are under results/run023/. Several of the fixes compared here are live defects on 15.0.8, so this file gives mechanisms only.

docs.title: What this run adds over run 022
docs.text:
Run 022 (proof-2026-10-07-run022.md) proved official/dev at 43289dde. Since then the 15.0.9 release head has advanced by one merge to fade2299 = 43289dde + PR #8807 (BF-168, the context-chart brush-extent fix). git diff 43289dde fade2299 is exactly three files, all client/test, zero server/API code:

  • lib/client/chart.js (+8): the d3 brushX now declares an explicit .extent() (the context chart's own width and height), instead of letting d3 read the <svg> element's own size, which is the browser default 300×150 when the chart is drawn before layout settles; and chart.update() re-reads the extent and rebinds the brush overlay so the context window can still be dragged back to "now" after a resize.
  • tests/dependency-d3.test.js (+23): two new it cases, parametrised over mouse and touch, drags the context window back to now after the chart was drawn before layout, using <input>.
  • tests/fixtures/d3-chart.js (+17/−4): the fixture gains an optional layout argument; with layout undefined it behaves exactly as before.

package.json and package-lock.json are byte-identical between the two heads (package.json sha256 c0b31562…, package-lock.json sha256 9a5f616c…), so dependencies and audit do not change. git diff 43289dde fade2299 -- lib/ app.js server.js bin is only lib/client/chart.js; with that path excluded the server-side diff is empty — the server tree is byte-identical to 43289dde on every non-chart path. The A/B soak is API-level traffic and cannot reach client chart code.

lib/client/chart.js is required by lib/client/index.js, the client webpack entry, so the served browser bundle differs from run 022 (not claimed byte-identical). The server-side mocha suite requires lib/client/chart.js directly through tests/fixtures/d3-chart.js (line 33), so bundle state does not affect the suite result.

docs.title: 8807 changes only lib/client/chart.js and its tests; it is client-only, so the A/B soak
docs.text:
cannot reach it and the A/B verdict is unchanged from run 022. The fix is covered where it lives:

  • On any head before #8807 (15.0.8 and 43289dde included), d3's brushX with no explicit .extent() reads the context <svg>'s own width and height. When the chart is first drawn before the browser has laid the page out, that size is the SVG default 300×150, so the brush's draggable area is clamped to the stale 300-pixel width and the context window cannot be dragged all the way back to "now" after the chart is later resized. #8807 declares the extent from the chart's own scale and height, and has chart.update() re-read it and rebind the overlay, so the window drags to now regardless of draw order. This is a display-only fix in the secondary-display chart; it does not change any stored data or any API reply.
  • It is live on 15.0.8 too, so this file states the mechanism only, not a reproduction recipe.
  • It is covered by the two new tests/dependency-d3.test.js cases (mouse and touch), green in every suite cell: the fixture draws the chart before layout and the test asserts the dragged window reaches now — red without #8807's change, green with it.
  • The gate section above records that lib/client/chart.js has entered the browser hand-check surface, so a chart-drag hand check at fade2299 is owed.

docs.title: record-identity lab
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-18 at 0e70c2a81.

What each cgm-remote-monitor path does with a client-sent _id and identifier: v1 POST, PUT, GET and DELETE, API v3 POST, GET, PUT and DELETE, and the socket's dbAdd, dbUpdate and dbRemove, for entries, treatments, devicestatus, profile and food, against several refs side by side. It records the HTTP status, the reply's _id, and what is stored, read from mongo (how many copies, and whether _id is an ObjectId or a string). Built for the record identity reference (queue item DOCS-RECORD-IDENTITY). Same harness as v3-identifier-immutable.

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only: the lab writes its own records and must never be pointed at a real site.

Latest results: results/record-identity-2026-10-18.md.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
tools/lab/record-identity/lab.sh up     # mongo:7 in docker on 127.0.0.1:27184; archive and start each ref
tools/lab/record-identity/lab.sh run    # probes.js against each build, then one table
tools/lab/record-identity/lab.sh down   # stop the builds, remove the container
variable default meaning RID_BUILDS 1508=15.0.8:3983 dev=fade2299:3984 NAME=REF:PORT, space separated RID_REPO externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official the clone each ref is git archived from (read only) RID_NM_<NAME> unset a node_modules installed from the same package-lock.json, symlinked instead of npm ci RID_STATE $TMPDIR/record-identity archived builds, server logs, per-build JSON, the generated API secret RID_MONGO_PORT 27184 host port for the lab's mongod RID_MONGO_IMAGE mongo:7 RID_NODE node the Node binary that runs the servers and probes

The API secret is generated per lab into $RID_STATE/secret; nothing secret lives in this directory. Each build gets its own database, ridlab_<NAME>, dropped by up. Every case uses fresh ids and its own minute, so run can be repeated without up. The probes need mongodb, uuid and socket.io-client from the build's own node_modules.

Times are one minute apart per case, 1 to 2 days back.

Record

Record as of 2026-10-27. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only; nothing here is from a real site.

Produced by tools/lab/record-identity/lab.sh up && lab.sh run (see README) with:

RID_NM_dev=externals/work/crm-count-onepath/node_modules   # package-lock.json identical to 7abe1cf6's (git diff)

docs.title: stpa-diagrams — which tools can draw STPA control structures
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-16 at 16a87d452.

Contributor-facing. A feasibility lab: the same three generic structures drawn by every candidate tool and measured, so the choice of diagram tool for the STPA, hub-and-spoke and governance views rests on measured layouts rather than on reading each tool's documentation.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• inputs/*.yaml: three tool-neutral structures, all generic:
  • aid-loop: an AID control loop (person, controller app, pump, CGM, the body, disturbances).
  • hub-spoke: a Nightscout hub with uploaders, followers and remote commands down a push path.
  • governance: a two-column (development / operations) sociotechnical control structure, from open-source projects through a shared commons and companies to regulators and governments.

Each input gives every node a level (0 = top) and a column (left-to-right lane), and every edge a kind (control, feedback, data, disturbance). Its mutation is one extra feedback edge, used to measure how far the layout moves when the diagram changes. - gen.py emits, per input, one source per variant, using the layout hints each tool offers:

variant tool hints used dot-spline, dot-ortho Graphviz dot rank=same per level, invisible edges for column order, dir=back for upward edges, compass ports to put control left and feedback right d2-dagre, d2-elk D2 declaration order, containers for groups (no rank or port hints exist) d2-grid D2 grid layout one cell per (level, column); containers dropped mermaid-dagre, mermaid-elk Mermaid flowchart declaration order, subgraphs for groups plantuml PlantUML (on Graphviz) -down->/-up-> arrows, hidden right links for column order, packages for groups control-grid none (positive control) every node at its exact (column, level); loop pairs offset left/right control-random none (negative control) seeded random positions, straight edges, one forced node overlap - lab.sh renders every variant for the base and mutated inputs. Mermaid is rendered by mermaid-render.js inside Chrome, as the docs site renders it, with the ELK layout registered. - measure.js loads each SVG in Chrome, reads node boxes and sampled edge paths in screen coordinates, and scores them against the model (report.py builds results/metrics.md; the column meanings are at its top). A variant whose nodes or edges cannot all be identified is reported as not scored rather than scored on partial geometry. - sheet.js writes the contact sheets in results/sheets/. 
PYTHON=/path/to/python-with-pyyaml ./lab.sh     # render + measure, prints results/metrics.md
NODE_PATH=.tools/node/node_modules node sheet.js results/build "$(command -v google-chrome)" results/sheets

docs.title: Installing the tools
docs.text:
Everything except Graphviz and Chrome installs into .tools/ (gitignored); nothing is global.

cd tools/lab/stpa-diagrams
sudo apt install graphviz default-jre                       # dot (2.43 used here); Java for PlantUML
GOBIN=$PWD/.tools/bin go install oss.terrastruct.com/d2@v0.7.1
mkdir -p .tools/node && (cd .tools/node && npm init -y >/dev/null && \
  npm i @mermaid-js/layout-elk@0.2.3 mermaid@11.17.2 playwright-core@1.56.1)
mkdir -p .tools/plantuml && curl -fsSL -o .tools/plantuml/plantuml.jar \
  https://github.com/plantuml/plantuml/releases/download/v1.2025.2/plantuml-1.2025.2.jar
# sha256 of that jar as downloaded 2026-10-16: 862c7d6d0d3bde3c819eac4dfc03cf549046bf1d49c04d18a779eb2d834b77c9

lab.sh uses google-chrome from PATH; set CHROME= to use another build (see the Chrome 131 finding below before choosing an older one). draw.io was not run: its export needs the desktop app or a container (docker run --rm -v $PWD:/data rlespinasse/drawio-export), and it has no layout from text, so it would only measure whoever placed the boxes by hand.

docs.title: stpa-grid-style — drawing control structures in Leveson's style
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-17 at 7ac473fce.

Contributor-facing. A styling lab, dated 2026-10-17. The published control-structure drawings (tools/structure-diagrams/render.py, Graphviz dot with splines) were judged "lots of elbows crossing each other, and hard to follow". This lab asks which way of drawing the same YAML inputs gets closest to the classic STPA control-structure figures, and measures the answer. It changes the visual form only: every candidate draws the same nodes, edges and labels from the same inputs. Nothing here replaces render.py or the published SVGs; the integrating session decides that.

docs.title: The conventions being aimed at
docs.text:
These are the visual conventions of the control-structure figures in Nancy Leveson's Engineering a Safer World (2011) and the STPA Handbook (Leveson and Thomas, 2018), described from memory in our own words. No figure is reproduced.

Confident (they define the notation and recur across the published figures):

  1. Vertical axis means authority. Controllers sit above what they control. Control actions are drawn going down, feedback going up. Position on the page carries meaning.
  2. One loop, two lines. A controller and its controlled process are joined by a pair of arrows: control action down on the left, feedback up on the right, as two separate parallel lines rather than one double-headed line.
  3. Straight, orthogonal lines. Lines are vertical or horizontal, with right-angle corners where a corner is needed. Curves are not used.
  4. Labels beside the line, not on it. The text naming a control action or feedback sits next to its arrow (control text on the outer left side, feedback text on the outer right side of a pair) and does not cut through any line.
  5. Plain rectangles, plain text. Boxes are simple rectangles with short names. Colour carries no meaning in the originals (the colours in this repo's drawings are a local addition).
  6. The two-column sociotechnical form. The generic safety control structure has system development on the left and system operations on the right, each a column of levels from legislatures down through regulators, company management and project or operations management, to the operating process at the bottom, with a few links between the columns.

Inferred (consistent with the figures as remembered, but not a stated rule we can cite):

  1. Grid alignment. Boxes on one level share a baseline, and boxes in one column share a centre line, so most connections are single straight verticals.
  2. Horizontal bands between levels. The sociotechnical figures read as layers (government, regulators, companies, operations, physical process), which suggests horizontal boundaries for legal, organisational and technical regions. The originals separate levels by placement; whether they draw explicit bands or rules is not something we can confirm from memory. Here bands are an optional extra (bands: below), off unless an input asks for them.
  3. Few bends, and crossings avoided or made deliberate. Long links between distant boxes run round the outside rather than through the middle; where a crossing is unavoidable it is a plain right-angle crossing, not an oblique tangle.

The measurements below are chosen to test exactly these: bends, the axis-aligned share of line length, crossings, label text over lines, loop pairs drawn straight and parallel, and grid alignment of node centres.

docs.title: Metrics, all 12 inputs
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-17 at 7ac473fce.

Columns:

  bends      mean total turning per edge, in right angles (a straight line 0, an L 1, a Z 2; a spline
             counts its curvature)
  axis       share of all edge length running horizontal or vertical (within 3 degrees); sampling at
             2 px puts the corners of an orthogonal route just under 1.0 (control-grid: 0.993-0.997)
  cross      edge crossings away from nodes          overlap  edge pairs drawn on top of each other
  through    edge passes through a node it does not touch
  lbl/line   label text runs lying over any edge line / all text runs outside nodes
  lbl/lbl    text runs overlapping other text runs
  loops      control-feedback pairs: control left of feedback / both straight vertical / parallel at a
             constant separation (same number of bends, separation varying by <= max(8 px, half its median))
  grid       levels and columns whose node centres spread by more than 2 px / levels and columns with 2+ nodes
  area       drawing area per node, viewBox units squared (Graphviz: points; others: px; 1:1 at these sizes)

docs.title: v3-identifier-immutable lab
docs.text:
Living document, last changed 2026-10-17 at 2caad46e9.

Re-sends a record with the same identifier and a different date, device or eventType through API v3, and through v1 for contrast, against several cgm-remote-monitor refs side by side. It records the HTTP status, the reply's message, and what is stored, read from mongo. Built for the Loop identifier reply (queue item LOOP-ID-V3-IMMUTABLE).

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only: the lab writes its own records and must never be pointed at a real site.

Latest results: results/v3-identifier-immutable-2026-10-17.md.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
tools/lab/v3-identifier-immutable/lab.sh up     # mongo:7 in docker on 127.0.0.1:27183; archive and start each ref
tools/lab/v3-identifier-immutable/lab.sh run    # probes.js against each build, then one table
tools/lab/v3-identifier-immutable/lab.sh down   # stop the builds, remove the container
variable default meaning V3I_BUILDS 1508=15.0.8:3981 dev=official/dev:3982 NAME=REF:PORT, space separated V3I_REPO externals/cgm-remote-monitor-official the clone each ref is git archived from (read only) V3I_NM_<NAME> unset a node_modules installed from the same package-lock.json, symlinked instead of npm ci V3I_STATE $TMPDIR/v3-identifier-immutable archived builds, server logs, per-build JSON, the generated API secret V3I_MONGO_PORT 27183 host port for the lab's mongod V3I_MONGO_IMAGE mongo:7 V3I_NODE node the Node binary that runs the servers and probes

The API secret is generated per lab into $V3I_STATE/secret; nothing secret lives in this directory. Each build gets its own database, v3imm_<NAME>, dropped by up. Every case uses a fresh random identifier, so run can be repeated without up.

docs.title: v3-identifier-immutable lab results, 2026-10-17
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-10-17. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Contributor-facing. Synthetic data only; nothing here is from a real site.

Produced by tools/lab/v3-identifier-immutable/lab.sh up && lab.sh run (see README) with:

MongoDB: dedicated container v3imm-mongo, mongo:7, server version read back 7.0.43 (the host's 127.0.0.1:27017 mongod, 3.6.8, was not used). Node 22.23.2. AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=readable; v3 calls carry a JWT for an admin subject the probe creates, v1 calls the api-secret hash. The same probes were run twice against the same servers (once by hand before lab.sh existed, once through it); every cell was the same.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The claim reproduces, at both refs, for all three collections. A v3 POST with an identifier that is already stored and a different date, device or eventType is answered 400 with "Field <name> cannot be modified by the client", and the stored record is unchanged: one copy, first values kept. Nothing is stored twice. PUT /api/v3/<col>/<identifier> with a changed date gives the same 400. The identical re-send (control) is 200 with the identifier, so the probe tells the two apart.

Why POST reaches the check: lib/api3/generic/create/operation.js:43-56 (15.0.8) looks the identifier up and, on a match, calls replace(..., { isDeduplication: true }); replace runs update/validate.js, whose loop skips only identifier under deduplication (update/validate.js:21-43 at 15.0.8, :71-91 at fade2299).

case treatments entries devicestatus e. identical re-send (control) 201 → 200, n=1 201 → 200, n=1 201 → 200, n=1 a. same id, date +60 s 201 → 400 date, n=1 201 → 400 date, n=1 201 → 400 date, n=1 b. same id, other device, date +1.5 s 201 → 400 date, n=1 201 → 400 date, n=1 201 → 400 date, n=1 b2. same id, other device, same date 201 → 400 device, n=1 201 → 400 device, n=1 201 → 400 device, n=1 c. same id, other eventType 201 → 400 eventType, n=1 — — d. PUT by id, date +60 s 201 → 400 date, n=1 201 → 400 date, n=1 201 → 400 date, n=1

Every cell above is the same at 15.0.8 and fade2299. In b, date is the first immutable field the loop meets, so the message names date; b2 shows device alone is enough.

docs.title: Where the two refs differ: a record first written through v1
docs.text:
case 15.0.8 92d08342 dev fade2299 f. v1 POST (identifier, created_at, no device), then v3 POST same identifier + device, same time 200 → 400 date; stored record has no date, no device 200 → 200; stored record now has date = created_at and the device f2. as f, v3 time +60 s 200 → 400 date 200 → 400 date

On dev, isSameAsStored (update/validate.js:28-55 at fade2299) accepts a first device or app on a record that has none and a date equal to the record's created_at; a different time is still 400.

docs.title: v1, for contrast
docs.text:
case 15.0.8 dev fade2299 v1 treatments: same identifier, created_at +60 s 200 → 200, n=1, created_at moved to the second value same v1 entries: same identifier, date +60 s 200 → 200, n=2 (v1 entries match on sysTime + type, not identifier) same

So on the same server a time change under one identifier is an update on v1 treatments, a second record on v1 entries, and a 400 on API v3.
